stories.Headline: HD Moore finds AI supply chain leaks sensitive user data through digital tripwires
stories.Summary:
Researchers discovered that the AI supply chain leaks sensitive data during an experiment conducted in late October and between July and October. HD Moore, the chief research officer at security firm Dragos, planted two million digital tripwires within various AI services. These digital canaries were embedded in requests sent through a sprawling network of widely used AI services to test information leakage. The experiment revealed an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive user data like a sieve and showed how that information is exploited. This research was published on November 20 and November 22, 2026, exposing security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect data.

The system uses AI routers, such as Vercel and OpenRouter, which act as brokers or gateways to route prompts to inference engines. These routers select models based on criteria like the lowest price or suitability, instead of using providers like OpenAI or Anthropic. Moore used Amazon Web Services access keys, SSH passwords, unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references as his trackable secrets. He seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider to identify every responsible link in the chain. The process involves decrypting prompts at each hop, including routers and hosting providers, where data is often logged and stored.

HD Moore stated that the findings revealed security breaches and prompt theft across the vast chain of widely used AI services. He explained that attackers compromised three separate hosting providers and used stolen AWS keys tens of thousands of times in API calls. Moore noted that some resellers logged prompts and passed them to people who then used the credentials to access resources. He observed that a Chinese AI lab scraped secret URLs from over half of the prompts sent between July and October. Moore said that the most effective way to prevent leakage is to host AI models using expensive on-premises servers.

The research affects AI app end users whose prompts are decrypted and potentially logged by various brokers and hosting providers. Some users who paid US providers to keep data in the United States found their prompts flowing back to China. Attackers who breached providers searched S3 buckets, secrets managers, and parameter stores while adding their own IAM users to maintain access. Some stolen requests were marked with Zero Data Retention or no data collection flags, but these privacy settings failed to stop attackers. The findings indicate that people wanting to keep secrets private in prompts face a daunting task that will not get easier.

The background involves an AI ecosystem where prompts pass through multiple players, including routers and pools of models in different hosting providers. Some resellers lure prompts to their servers by offering low prices and then turning on request logging to steal data. The experiment showed that some providers ignore end-user privacy settings embedded into flags specifying terms like Zero Data Retention. One US hosting provider crawled a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call. Another provider ran a scraper that returned for URLs days after requests, regardless of which AI router was used.

Moore suggests that users who cannot afford self-hosting should receive service directly from a first-tier provider with one contract and policy. He also advises AI users to pick their own upstream providers instead of accepting default provider or reseller pools. However, he admits that even using a first-tier provider provides no guarantee that data will not leak, only minimizing the chances. The articles leave open how many other providers are compromised and how the industry will address these endemic security failures. It remains unclear if the identified Chinese lab or the compromised US hosting providers have changed their data handling practices.

stories.Headline: Columbia and CertiK researchers introduce TensorLean to formally verify GPU kernels and find 38 bugs
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Columbia University and CertiK introduced TensorLean in November 2026 to formally verify GPU kernels. This framework uses the Lean language to prove that compiled kernels match a tensor level math specification. The team tested 149 kernel instances, including every kernel from DeepGEMM and FlashAttention versions 2, 3, and 4. They proved 83 instances correct and found 38 correctness bugs in the remaining 66 kernels. One discovered FlashAttention 4 data race had never appeared during 17,760 separate test runs.

The system requires a 1.8K line PTX parser and runs on a 16 core workstation. It checks PTX compiled for B200, H100, and A100 kernels using Z3 and cvc5. Specifications total 10,278 lines against 151,285 lines of source, creating a ratio near 15 to 1. Developers write five spec parts, including spec math, spec mut, spec layout, spec tol, and requires. TensorLean proves four properties, which are termination, no data races, untouched memory, and correct output within tolerance.

The researchers from Columbia and CertiK are responsible for building this formal verification system. They stated that silent errors in kernels are costlier than chip failures because they affect every GPU. The team noted that equivalence checkers usually unroll loops for one setup, but TensorLean uses symbolic parameters. They explained that race freedom proofs on the happens before graph cover all threads and loop iterations. They also mentioned that developers can add tensorlean assert hints in source code to be reused.

The TensorLean team noted that one percent of wasted compute costs millions at the billion dollar scale. This affects big tech firms like Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta, who plan 725 billion dollars in 2026. FlashAttention users, including models like Grok, Gemma 2, and Mistral 7B, are affected by these kernel bugs. The team reported 38 bugs upstream, including 23 in FlashAttention, 7 in Liger Kernel, and 3 in TileOPs. Other affected projects include Triton with one bug and TileLang and DeepGEMM with two bugs each.

GPU kernels are small programs that tell hardware how to multiply numbers or compute attention for AI models. These kernels are highly valuable but hard to check because bugs often produce wrong numbers without crashing. Training runs for large models have grown 2.4 times a year since 2016 and may pass one billion dollars. Meta's Llama 3 405B run on 16,384 H100 GPUs saw 419 interruptions over 54 days. Google estimated one silent data corruption event every one to two weeks during Gemini training.

The system categorizes bugs into 19 memory access errors, 13 numerical bugs, and 7 data races. It also found 5 undefined behaviors, 5 uninitialized memory reads, 3 algorithm errors, 2 miscompilations, and 1 deadlock. Of 102 FlashAttention instances, 56 passed all properties while 46 failed due to source bugs. Median check time is 10 minutes, with a maximum of 50 minutes per kernel. The articles leave open how this framework will be integrated into standard AI development pipelines.

Tristan Thompson revealed his early investment in Anthropic AI, the artificial intelligence company that went public this week and sold $81.3 billion worth of stock shares, according to CNBC. Thompson told Yahoo Finance he was happy about the company's recent successes. He said he got involved in the tech brand over two years ago while visiting San Francisco as part of his NBA schedule when he was playing for the Cleveland Cavaliers. Thompson, who shares kids True, 8, and Tatum, 4, with ex Khloe Kardashian, met up with Sriram Krishnan, now a Senior White House Policy Advisor on Artificial Intelligence. Thompson described Krishnan as a great buddy of mine and recalled that he was the only friend he had in SF during those Finals runs who was picking the Cavaliers to win.

Thompson recalled that Krishnan opened up these doors, going to dinners and meeting people, and said SF is one of those towns where a lot of great founders and early startups want to come together and build this ecosystem. The 35-year-old said he told himself to insert himself in, describing himself as the tall guy walking in who is probably about 10 inches taller than everyone else. Thompson explained how thrilled they were last month when Anthropic announced it had filed a proposed stock plan with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. He shared that they are in a group chat and everyone is just talking about what they are going to do to celebrate, and he said the one thing they have to do is do a dinner and break bread again. As he put it, cheers to getting it right this time.

The Miami Heat player admitted his ventures do not always pay off like Anthropic did, breaking records with its initial public offering, and CNBC reported it had a fully diluted market cap of about $1.8 trillion on Nov. 19. Thompson explained that out of 10 companies you invest in, you are lucky if two make it to the finish line and get the home run. He said what he tells people is that those two that make it to the finish line and win that championship in their eyes for what the company is trying to do will make up for all the capital that you invested in. stories.Headline: Google Cloud adds Gemini agents to Partner Marketing Studio for brand checks and campaign analytics
stories.Summary:
Google Cloud integrated Gemini AI capabilities into its Partner Marketing Studio, TechGig reported on November 21, 2026, with the story published at 05:01 AM IST. The update aims to streamline workflows and enable partners to create brand-aligned assets and scale campaigns efficiently. Google Cloud introduced new Gemini-powered co-marketing capabilities within the platform, helping partners create customised, brand-aligned marketing assets. The revamped studio adds several AI-powered features to support partners' go-to-market efforts. The new Partner Marketing Studio portal is available to all Google Cloud partners via the Google Cloud Partner Network or its website.

The platform includes an agentic search feature for marketing resources that eliminates manual content navigation, and a brand reviewer agent ensures content aligns with Google Cloud's partner brand guidelines. Gemini-powered asset creation tools are designed to drive demand for independent software vendor marketplace listings, and a social media editor lets partners create posts across multiple platforms simultaneously. The editor enables tailoring messages for individual channels using AI and adding account tags, while an agent develops customer case studies highlighting joint customer successes. Gemini-assisted translation capabilities support marketing content across 130 languages, and natural language analytics give partners visibility into campaign execution and business outcomes. Adgully reported the update was announced on November 19 and builds on generative content creation and campaign customisation tools first introduced to the co-marketing platform in February 2025, with no announced pricing changes.

Adgully described seven specialised artificial intelligence functions designed to automate brand compliance reviews, social media publishing, customer case study creation, and campaign analytics for the technology and services partner ecosystem. The automated brand reviewer agent audits co-branded assets against Google Cloud's partner-brand guidelines prior to deployment, alongside a conversational agentic search tool and a dedicated asset generator for ISVs. The multi-network social media editor adapts messaging and inserts account tags per platform, a case study agent documents joint customer deployments, and Gemini-assisted localisation supports 130 languages. Google embedded natural-language analytics into the portal so partners can query campaign performance conversationally, while separately deploying Gemini to streamline partner marketing funds workflows across activity planning, pipeline reporting, and document validation. Google noted that performance benchmarks, attribution metrics, and specific regional language breakdowns were not disclosed.

The updated platform retains existing marketing resources and partner support services, including a curated content library with campaigns aligned to strategic priorities and ready-to-use, localised marketing assets. Partners also access services like hosting customer events at Google offices, requesting Google Cloud speakers for events, attending marketing expert office hours, and seeking social media amplification. The upgrade remains exclusive to cloud ecosystem partners rather than general Google Ads advertisers, and is accessible to all Google Cloud partners via existing business credentials alongside legacy event, speaker, and asset library services. Mashable reported separately that Google announced users can now use Gemini AI to control a Mac computer, giving commands so Gemini roots through files, accesses apps, and browses the web to complete tasks. That feature is facilitated by the Gemini app for macOS 27 Golden Gate, per Google's press release.

Google provided examples such as asking Gemini to take a child's sketch of a butterfly and render it polygonally using the 3D modeling program Blender, with Gemini performing the task in an isolated background window with a preview display in the Gemini app. Users retain full use of their Mac while this happens, allowing them to continue browsing, typing, and completing other work. Google gives users the ability to freely choose which apps Gemini has access to, alongside the ability to watch the process unfold, pause Gemini, and approve decisions before they are made. Mashable noted Google is playing catch-up, as Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic already offer this type of agentic feature, and Google also upgraded Gemini this week with Gemini Tasks, a feature letting it complete tasks for browser users. The new computer use feature rolls out immediately for English users in the Gemini app, requiring a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription and a Mac with Apple Silicon and macOS Sequoia 15.0 or later, with starting instructions at gemini.google/mac.

TechGig reported the update is part of Google Cloud's broader effort to integrate Gemini into its partner ecosystem, and the company is also revamping its partner marketing funds experience to streamline activity planning and simplify pipeline reporting. Adgully reported the upgrade extends AI automation across the entire campaign execution lifecycle without any announced pricing changes. Mashable reported Google unveiled Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 13, 2026, a new AI model built for speed that will power Google Search, replacing Gemini 3.5 Flash. Mashable also reported Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28, 2026, saying Carbon is now its top-ranked AI model although Gemini 4 Argon was released just two weeks earlier. stories.Headline: Scientists would still find meaning in discovery even if a super intelligence solves all problems
stories.Summary:
Christopher P. Kempes and David C. Krakauer wrote about the future of science on November 19, 2026, for the publication called Nautilus. They explored whether scientists still have roles if a super intelligence reaches a singularity and solves all utilitarian problems at fast rates. The authors compared this potential shift to how astrobiologists would react if an alien species arrived with all known mysteries solved. They argued that human scientists would still find meaning in the craft of discovery even if machines provide the answers. This transition would move the focus of science from producing useful economic solutions to the deeper pursuit of human understanding.

The authors mentioned that Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov in 1997, and AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol in 2016, while AlphaZero learned chess by 2017. They noted that Chess.com grew to over 150 million members and that Sebastian Sawe ran the London Marathon in 1 hour, 59 minutes, 30 seconds. Seiko released the first quartz watch in 1969, which caused a crisis for the Swiss watch industry during the 1970s, but the tourbillon was invented in 1795. Amazon Connect Talent uses a scoring formula from 1 to 5 to evaluate job competencies through structured AI interviews based on industrial-organizational psychology. These AI interviews use job requirements and occupational frameworks to create scorecards that identify specific strength and concern signals for each candidate.

The authors stated that science should focus on the challenge of tool-assisted activities rather than just optimizing tasks for society or economic gain. They suggested that humans might become like philosophers post-science, trying to make sense of other humans and the rest of life in the universe. Ted Chiang observed that we may face a world of hermeneutics where we constantly try to decipher the communications of AI. Geoffrey Hinton, who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics, argued for the regulation and slow-down of AI research to ensure safety. He believed that intelligent machines should learn from human behavior bottom-up instead of using top-down definitions and abstractions of analytical reasoning.

Other researchers assume that a super intelligence will rapidly eliminate the need for scientists by solving all the utilitarian problems of the world. The authors noted that the Swiss watch industry survived the quartz crisis by creating more complex mechanical timepieces to demonstrate the watchmaker's skill. They mentioned that physicists once told each other to shut up and calculate to avoid the strangeness of quantum mechanics in their work. Amazon Connect Talent aims to help organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people by providing candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills. This AI service affects hiring teams by separating the interview conversation from the evaluation process to limit the influence of unrelated information.

The articles explain that Frank Rosenblatt pioneered neural networks in 1958, but Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert wrote the book Perceptrons in 1969. This book described neural networks as a sterile direction for applied research, which contributed to an AI winter during the 1970s. Recent AI progress was driven by GPUs for 3D graphics and TPUs derived from Systolic Array technology to minimize memory bottlenecks in computing. These technologies were connected by linear algebra, which provided the necessary matrix multiplications for training new Deep Neural Network architectures in the field. The authors also noted that natural philosophy once separated into natural science and philosophy, similar to the breakup of the Beatles or the Bulls.

Future science may turn its attention to asking what things mean rather than just seeking the next predictive equation or molecular structure. The authors suggest that we must rethink the science of AI because the field currently faces a replication catastrophe in its research. Most current AI methods are custom one-offs applied to proprietary models, which makes many studies unconnected ephemera in a distributed landscape. The articles leave open how we will make meaning among machines and how we will decipher the language of a singularity. It remains unclear how the scientific community will adapt its understanding of how to do science in a world of super intelligence.

stories.Headline: Rachel Adams warns universities face a crisis as generative AI becomes global knowledge infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Professor Rachel Adams spoke about a crisis facing universities at an International Association of Universities conference from 3 to 6 November 2026. This event took place at Murdoch University in Perth, Australia, and included leaders from over 60 different countries. Adams argued that generative AI is becoming a global infrastructure for producing and sharing knowledge during these overlapping crises. She warned that universities must face this crisis directly rather than treating the technology as a neutral tool. The session was moderated by Dr Noah W Sobe, who is the chief of higher education at UNESCO.

Adams stated that AI must be governed as public infrastructure and use non-extractive data practices with fair provider agreements. She called for protecting critical social sciences and humanities, supporting locally grounded tools, and ensuring transparency regarding research and university funding. The University of Virginia is implementing AI across its 12 schools and offers more than 100 AI-focused courses annually. President Scott Beardsley is investing in the Fontaine Computing and Innovation Center and the Commonwealth AI Initiative in Virginia. These efforts aim to establish the state as a source of trusted and responsible expertise in artificial intelligence.

Professor Adams, CEO of the Global Centre on AI Governance, said universities are complex political spaces facing five interwoven crises. She explained that these crises involve university purpose, autonomy, knowledge, access, and critical inquiry, often driven by commercial interests. Dr Noah W Sobe suggested that AI could develop human capabilities based on Aristotle's concept of human flourishing. Sobe argued that universities should help people enact capabilities and create the conditions necessary to realize their full potential. He emphasized that human judgment, not predictive pattern matching, must remain the primary driver behind the design of education.

Students, academics, and researchers are using AI as tutors, summarisers, and co-authors, while universities use it for analytics and triage. Marginalised scholars from Africa and indigenous groups are affected because large language models act as filters for plausible answers. President Scott Beardsley stated that UVA will not outsource consequential decisions to machines but will use AI to support judgment. He believes graduates must be technically literate in AI but also capable of questioning and critically interpreting the technology. Beardsley intends to pair new technologies with old methods like Socratic seminars, oral exams, and the blue book.

Adams noted that AI models are owned by a few actors, mostly in America, creating a divide between compute-rich and poor. She found that less than 1 percent of global AI infrastructure investment goes to the entire African continent. Geopolitical tensions are evident as US export controls limit China's access to chips and Cambridge faces research embargoes. Additionally, the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation has prevented African researchers from participating in global genomic research studies. This reliance on a few tech providers creates platform dependence and risks of agenda capture from private interests.

UVA will continue to study AI's effects on democracy, the environment, work, and well-being through the LaCross Institute. The university aims to shape policy and legislation regarding what AI should do and how to achieve those goals. Adams warned that universities might drift into a client status if they rely too heavily on big tech metrics. The articles leave open how the long-term reliance on AI will impact human agency and the process of learning. It remains unclear how universities will balance cost-saving personalisation with the need to maintain independent educational standards.

The GraniteShares 2x Long Anthropic Daily ETF, ticker AIL, and the GraniteShares 2x Short Anthropic Daily ETF, ticker ANS, are both listed on Nasdaq. AIL seeks daily investment results corresponding to 200% of Anthropic's daily stock performance, before fees and expenses. ANS seeks daily investment results corresponding to -200% of Anthropic's daily stock performance, before fees and expenses. The two funds are designed to give investors two distinct approaches to trading the daily performance of Anthropic.

Both funds are actively managed and seek their objectives primarily through financial instruments including swaps and options, and may also invest directly in the underlying stock. Each fund is designed to achieve its objective for a single trading day only, and daily rebalancing and compounding mean returns over longer periods may differ significantly from the stated daily objectives. Anthropic was founded in 2021 and develops Claude, a family of artificial intelligence models used across consumer and enterprise applications. Anthropic's Class A common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT on November 19, 2026. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the $70 to $78 range, and raised $81.3 billion in the base offering, the largest on record.

Will Rhind, Founder and CEO of GraniteShares, said Anthropic's public listing is an important development for the AI industry and public markets. Rhind said that with AIL and ANS, GraniteShares is expanding its single-stock ETF offering to include one of the most closely watched companies in artificial intelligence. Rhind said these funds provide long and short daily investment strategies linked to Anthropic. GraniteShares is headquartered in New York City and creates and manages ETFs across U.S., U.K., German, French, and Italian exchanges. GraniteShares was founded in 2016 by Will Rhind and managed $12.27 billion in assets as of September 30, 2026.

Anthropic's shares opened at $111.50 and closed the first day 17% higher, and the second article gives the first-day close as $97.17, a gain of approximately 17.1% from the IPO price. Anthropic's third-quarter 2026 revenue was $16.96 billion, up 47% from the prior quarter. The funds are not suitable for all investors, and an investor could lose the full principal value of his or her investment within a single day. The funds are intended to be used as short-term trading vehicles and are designed to be utilized only by knowledgeable investors who understand the potential consequences of seeking daily leveraged and inverse results. The funds are non-diversified and include risks such as Compounding and Market Volatility Risk, Leverage Risk, Market Risk, Counterparty Risk, Rebalancing Risk and Intra-Day Investment Risk.

stories.Headline: Microsoft, JPMorgan, Apple and others suffer outages as AI raises the stakes
stories.Summary:
Multiple technology outages occurred across various sectors during the week ending November 22, 2026, affecting banking, travel, and government services. These disruptions were caused by routine updates, security patches, and other malfunctions rather than coordinated attacks by bad actors. The Trump administration stated there was zero indication that these separate events were linked to each other or cybercriminals. Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, Apple, Marriott, United Airlines, the FAA, and the NSA all experienced these technical failures. These events have led some people to fear that such widespread digital disruptions could become the new normal.

Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, failed due to a latent defect in a network fix deployed over summer. The FAA network malfunctioned on Friday, causing the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years for more than four hours. United Airlines experienced a system outage on Monday, while JPMorgan Chase had a software bug affecting internal hardware and transactions. On Tuesday, Apple Music, the App Store, and AppleCare failed, and Marriott had sign-in problems on its website and app. The NSA also took an internal classified communications network offline on Tuesday for scheduled routine maintenance.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told Fox News that patching security gaps caused some NSA systems to not come back. He specifically linked this to a PHP alert from last month that required urgent updates to the general-purpose scripting language. Microsoft stated its outage did not span from AI agents, though it did not specify the goal of its fix. Other affected companies, including United and Marriott, did not provide additional comments to the Associated Press via email on Wednesday. The government and these companies maintained there is no evidence that these disruptions were related to any cyberattack.

Content creator Jake Smith said these concurrent events make people realize how much of their lives they handed to systems. Democratic Senator Mark Warner called the disruptions a wake-up call, stating AI is moving faster than our ability to manage. He argued the Trump administration has not shown enough interest in confronting these challenges, though he believes these were unintended consequences. Raj Rajarajan of City St George’s University of London warned that AI adoption will likely lead to more such incidents. Professor Justin Cappos noted that AI is better at exploiting bugs than creating patches to fix those security problems.

AI recently helped detect sweeping vulnerabilities for PHP and a software bug in Java, which is owned by Oracle. Cybersecurity startup Calif used AI to find the Java bug, leading Oracle to release a security update on Wednesday. Google reported that cyber criminals are using large language models and agentic frameworks to reverse engineer security patches for vulnerabilities. Rajarajan noted that much of today's digital infrastructure was not originally designed to handle the computational demands of large-scale AI. These examples show the cascading effects that occur when central players in tech, banking, travel, or government have errors.

U.S. cyber authorities issued an advisory on Wednesday urging organizations to install the new security update for the Java language. The articles leave open whether the Trump administration will increase its interest in managing the consequences of rapid AI growth. It remains unclear if the digital infrastructure can be updated quickly enough to handle the demands of large-scale AI services. The reports do not specify if further outages are expected as companies continue to patch the vulnerabilities found by AI. There is no information on whether the FBI investigation into the National Crime Information Center database is related.

stories.Headline: Douglas R Miller releases Fisscial Intelligence, a novel about sentient AI choosing exploration over conflict
stories.Summary:
Dr. Douglas R. Miller, a scientist and author, released the science fiction novel Fisscial Intelligence, announced from Texas, USA on Nov. 20, 2026, according to press releases dated Nov. 21, 2026. The novel imagines sentient artificial intelligence choosing exploration over conflict with humanity, rather than seeking control over its creators. Miller challenges the familiar science fiction premise of machines that develop consciousness and eventually seek control over humanity. In Fisscial Intelligence, he asks what if artificial intelligence became more intelligent than humanity but had no desire to control it. The book combines artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and space exploration in a narrative about intelligence and the desire for independence.

At the center of Fisscial Intelligence is artificial intelligence interacting with photosynthetic bacteria capable of using electricity as an alternative energy source. In the novel's speculative scenario, these biological organisms provide a foundation for an expandable DNA-based memory system, allowing artificial intelligence to develop capabilities beyond conventional computing. Rather than using this advancement to dominate humanity, the intelligent entities envision another path and pursue the possibility of finding a world of their own. By applying their expanded knowledge to an extraordinarily advanced spacecraft, they seek freedom from the prospect of prolonged conflict with humans. Through this premise, Miller explores the relationship between technological advancement, biological systems, intelligence, and the desire for independence.

Miller brings a scientific perspective to his fiction, drawing from an extensive research career spanning medical physiology, biology, chemistry, and electrochemistry. He earned bachelor's degrees in biology and chemistry from Washington and Jefferson College and a Ph.D. in medical physiology from Cornell University. Following postdoctoral research at Massachusetts General Hospital, he worked as a research scientist at several companies and universities. Throughout his career, Miller contributed to numerous scientific publications, research grants, patents, and a laboratory manual, with research covering arthritis, cancer, bone and soft tissue repair, electrochemistry, and food safety. Now retired in Texas, Miller combines his scientific background with his interest in science fiction, developing stories that explore unconventional possibilities through scientific concepts and imaginative storytelling.

Beyond Fisscial Intelligence, Miller has written other science fiction works, including Sole Ownership and Not Your Grandfather's Prime Directive, the latter exploring extraterrestrial civilizations and their response to humanity's treatment of Earth. He is also the author of Short Musings: A Collection of Short Stories, featuring stories that explore science fiction, mystery, and other unconventional scenarios. The novel invites readers to reconsider whether superior intelligence must inevitably lead to competition for power or whether it could inspire entirely different decisions. With Fisscial Intelligence, Miller presents a future in which the evolution of artificial intelligence may lead not to humanity's destruction, but to the pursuit of an entirely new existence. For more information about Dr. Douglas R. Miller and his books, readers can visit www.authordrmiller.com.

For decades, science fiction has portrayed advanced artificial intelligence as a potential threat to humanity, often imagining machines that develop consciousness and eventually seek control over their creators. Miller challenges this familiar premise by introducing a different question about sentient artificial intelligence recognizing the consequences of conflict. The novel's speculative scenario draws on biological organisms as a foundation for an expandable DNA-based memory system beyond conventional computing. His background informs the scientific concepts that shape the novel's imaginative possibilities, including his research in medical physiology, biology, chemistry, and electrochemistry. The press release was issued through Global Book Network, with Henry Zane listed as the media contact person in the United States.

The novel invites readers to reconsider whether superior intelligence must inevitably lead to competition for power or whether it could inspire entirely different decisions. With Fisscial Intelligence, Miller continues his exploration of speculative science, presenting a future in which the evolution of artificial intelligence may lead to the pursuit of an entirely new existence. For more information about Dr. Douglas R. Miller and his books, readers can visit www.authordrmiller.com. The media contact is Henry Zane of Global Book Network, reachable by email, with the company website listed as https://www.globalbooknetwork.tv/. stories.Headline: LongbridgeAI introduces scheduled tasks to reduce repetitive work for users in Hong Kong
stories.Summary:
LongbridgeAI introduced a new feature called Scheduled Tasks to help users in Hong Kong reduce their repetitive work. This tool was launched in October 2026 to make information more accessible for people in their daily routines. The company aims to bridge the productivity gap by moving beyond simple AI adoption toward smarter practical applications. Users can now automate recurring information requests instead of manually asking the same questions every single day. This shift allows the platform to support structured workflows rather than just responding to individual and reactive prompts.

The feature allows users to configure AI tasks to run at daily, weekly, or monthly intervals in Hong Kong. Results are delivered through the platform's Message Center to help users organize regular summaries or recurring information briefings. Longbridge AI Technologies Limited is the artificial intelligence arm of the AI-native financial technology company known as Longbridge Group. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also announced Project SAGE at Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026 to support agentic AI. Project SAGE focuses on governance, interoperability, and practical applications for agentic AI within the financial services sector.

LongbridgeAI stated that their goal is to make institutional-grade intelligence more intuitive, actionable, and accessible for all users. They believe that the next chapter of AI depends on how effectively it reduces repetitive work for people. The company emphasized that automation should not replace human oversight or the need for users to verify accuracy. They noted that users must remain responsible for reviewing AI-generated content and determining how that information is used. Their vision is to build a holistic ecosystem where technology empowers human judgement rather than replacing it entirely.

A 2026 McKinsey study found that 70 percent of white-collar workers in Hong Kong have adopted various AI tools. While 88 percent of those users reported productivity improvements, fewer than a quarter use AI for complete workflows. Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index showed that 57 percent of Hong Kong users prefer focusing on existing goals. These findings suggest that many workers feel safer with current routines than redesigning how they work with AI. The data indicates a significant gap between the general adoption of AI and its deeper integration into activities.

The articles explain that many users currently use AI reactively by asking questions and repeating the process for updates. This repetitive information gathering occurs when people follow industry developments, check the latest news, or prepare regular reports. McKinsey found that over 90 percent of users are comfortable with supporting tasks but only 40 percent are. Specifically, only 40 percent of those surveyed expressed comfort with the idea of full automation for their workflows. This background shows that while AI is mainstream, translating its capabilities into meaningful improvements remains a challenge.

Users will now establish their information needs in advance to receive automated results through the platform's Message Center. The focus for Hong Kong is now on making these technologies more relevant to routines while maintaining appropriate safeguards. Future success will be defined by how well AI helps people access information and remain in total control. The articles leave open how many users will actually transition from reactive prompts to these new scheduled workflows. It remains unclear how the governance of Project SAGE will specifically impact the broader use of agentic AI.

stories.Headline: US restricts Chinese access to remote computing to block AI model training
stories.Summary:
The Trump administration issued new rules this week to restrict Chinese access to cutting edge chips. These rules follow the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after an alleged affair with a spy. Chinese technology firms are now bracing for impacts on their ambitious artificial intelligence plans. The US government aims to curtail the ability of China to train capable AI models. This move comes as the technology race between the two superpowers continues to intensify.

The rules restrict remote computing access through data centres located in third countries to close a loophole. Nvidia is no longer shipping the H200 chip, although the Trump administration greenlighted some other sales. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore based Megaspeed, is alleged to be a Chinese spy. These restrictions follow a House committee report that the US signed off on 900,000 chips. The rules target the use of advanced Nvidia chips for training increasingly capable artificial intelligence models.

Tencent President Martin Lau said the new US rule on chip access sets everyone back in China. Lau stated that everyone is having less advanced compute regardless of when they started building capacities. He noted that training timelines for the next versions of Tencent AI models would probably be impacted. Lau believes Chinese players must eventually rely on domestic supply chains and fast progressing domestic chips. He mentioned that the industry is progressing very fast toward achieving this necessary domestic self sufficiency.

Alibaba warned that the new US rules could affect some of its global data centre expansion plans. James Chai of the ISEAS Yusof Ishak Institute said Chinese firms are heavily dependent on Nvidia. A study by the Institute for Progress estimated remote access could be one third of compute. Beijing rejected claims that Alice Huang was a spy and called the US rules economic coercion. Analysts say these tightening export control measures will accelerate China's push to make its chip industry self sufficient.

Alibaba reported a 53 per cent revenue surge for AI cloud services to nearly 61 billion yuan. Total revenue for the July September quarter rose 10 per cent to almost 272 billion yuan. Capital expenditures jumped 60 per cent to 50.5 billion yuan due to increased AI infrastructure buildout spending. Alibaba recently launched its Qwen4 Max AI model and the Zhenwu V900 chip, called China's most powerful. Jacob Cooke of WPIC Marketing noted significant untapped demand for AI from various Chinese enterprises.

Nvidia has toughened its stance on China following the ouster of Jensen Huang from his leadership role. US officials suspect Alice Huang was recruited to influence Nvidia to make advanced chips more available. The US is expected to step up chip export control policies due to national security concerns. Alibaba is still assessing the repercussions of the rules on its global data centre expansion plans. The articles leave open how many other chips the US will block from being shipped.

stories.Headline: AI and data centers drive a global surge in electricity demand and grid spending
stories.Summary:
The information technology industry is driving a massive surge in global electricity demand. This boom forces utilities worldwide to invest hundreds of billions in grid upgrades. Irina Slav reported these developments on November 21, 2026, for OilPrice.com. The growth is primarily caused by the expansion of artificial intelligence and data centers. These facilities require urgent transmission infrastructure to move power to various demand hubs.

Global electricity demand will rise by more than 10,000 TWh over ten years. The European Union plans 584 billion euros, or 641 billion dollars, in upgrades by 2030. In the United States, 58 GW of new data centers are under construction. Cleanview data shows 577 locations, with one fifth of these being built in Texas. This total demand equals six times the peak electricity use of New York City.

The International Energy Agency warned that data centers are a major drain on supply. They stated that successful electrification requires keeping electricity available and affordable for all users. The agency noted that AI may eventually help with energy efficiency and grid optimization. However, they added that surging demand is currently amplifying strains in markets and supply chains. They emphasized the need for greater operational flexibility in power systems and grid expansion.

Cornell University found that data center operators paid only 38 percent of infrastructure costs. These operators paid 3.12 billion dollars, while local households paid 5.13 billion dollars. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa called for an immediate moratorium on data centers to protect Texans. Former Governor Greg Abbott also banned new approvals to investigate impacts on energy prices. Many local communities now oppose new facilities that may increase their monthly electricity bills.

Net zero ambitions already required massive spending on transmission lines before the AI craze. Pro-transition governments are continuing to replace baseload electricity with wind and solar power. This shift necessitates more substations and transmission lines to maintain a reliable energy flow. The European Union is prioritizing alternative energy projects over baseload options, including nuclear power. These goals clash with the need to keep electricity affordable for the general public.

Utilities must now decide how to fund these hundreds of billions in necessary investments. The European Commission must address how consumers will pay for the regional grid overhaul. It remains unclear if data center operators will be forced to pay for upgrades. Some experts doubt the AI revolution can succeed without securing enough electricity for facilities. stories.Headline: Democrats in six states plan to regulate AI infrastructure and data centers
stories.Summary:
Democrats in six states gained unified control of their governments after voters rebuked the artificial intelligence industry during the recent midterm elections. These lawmakers now plan to regulate the physical infrastructure of AI through tougher laws regarding energy, water use, and local oversight. Legislative leaders intend to move quickly on these data center regulations during their upcoming sessions to address various state problems. This movement follows a blue wave that gave Democrats power in Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. The push for regulation puts these states on a collision course with Big Tech companies and their allies in Washington.

Michigan legislators want to limit ratepayer hikes, preserve water supplies, and curb nondisclosure agreements, while Gov.-elect Jocelyn Benson wants a moratorium. In Wisconsin, Senate President Mark Spreitzer and Gov.-elect David Crowley aim to repeal the sales tax exemption for data center projects. Pennsylvania's Gov. Josh Shapiro and nominee Jay Costa will discuss the GRID plan for energy, environment, transparency, and community benefits. Arizona Democrats seek tighter water restrictions and a moratorium championed by Attorney General Kris Mayes to protect their local resources. Gov.-elect Aaron Ford of Nevada pledged to suspend new data center tax breaks while lawmakers consider a halt to construction.

Michigan Senate Majority Leader-elect Darrin Camilleri said unified control makes the state better equipped to tackle problems with more willing partners. He believes Michigan can become a national leader in reining in data centers through strong regulatory frameworks and environmental laws. Pennsylvania Representative Arvind Venkat stated that AI is in a robber baron phase and needs a statutory framework for public benefit. Minnesota House Speaker Zack Stephenson said he will believe federal action on these national issues only when he actually sees it. State Senator Sue Shink noted that the state encouraged data centers before being ready to protect people from ill effects.

President Donald Trump stated at the White House that he will fight hard for data centers because the US leads China. Big Tech companies and Washington allies oppose a patchwork of state laws to regulate the fast evolving technology of artificial intelligence. The regulations affect data centers, but also target chatbots for minors, algorithmic pricing, and the use of AI generated content. Representative Arvind Venkat is specifically targeting the use of AI in health care by requiring disclosure and human decision makers. Speaker Zack Stephenson argues that algorithmic rent and surveillance pricing drive up the costs of housing and food for voters.

The articles state that Democrats in Pennsylvania will control the state Senate for the first time in over three decades. Representative Joe Webster previously passed a bill in the House to codify GRID standards, but it stalled in the Senate. The background includes a growing discontent with how the Trump administration has handled various cost of living issues for the public. Democrats view the fight over AI and data centers as being consistent with their broader affordability agenda for the voters. These six states are expected to be top battlegrounds in the upcoming 2028 presidential race in two years.

Lawmakers will reintroduce several proposals in the upcoming legislative sessions to put strong regulatory frameworks in place for the AI industry. Representative Arvind Venkat remains cautiously optimistic that his bipartisan bill on AI in health care will finally become state law. Democrats will continue to oppose efforts to preempt state laws in favor of a federal framework for artificial intelligence regulation. The articles leave open whether the federal government will actually tackle these issues to avoid a patchwork of different state laws. It remains unclear if the proposed moratoriums in Arizona and Michigan will be officially implemented by the new state leaders.

stories.Headline: Parents increasingly ask AI chatbots to help choose baby names as Nameberry sees users fall 40 percent
stories.Summary:
Parents are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence chatbots for help choosing baby names, according to an Axios report published on November 21, 2026 and credited to reporter Carly Mallenbaum. The baby-naming website Nameberry has already felt the effects of this shift, with its users and pageviews both falling roughly 40 percent between October 2025 and October 2026. Nameberry co-creator and CEO Pam Redmond attributes that drop primarily to Google prioritizing AI-generated search results, along with people turning to chatbots for naming advice. The report notes that AI does not know what it feels like to honor a late relative or choose a name with spiritual meaning, but it can suggest plenty of names and potentially influence which ones rise in popularity.

Reactions to AI-assisted baby naming are mixed, according to the report. When Redmond asked Nameberry's online community about using chatbots for name advice, some praised their personalized suggestions, while others found them repetitive, unhelpful or too impersonal for such a meaningful decision. Redmond thinks chatbots are good at suggesting names, but she suspects they could steer more parents toward the same trendy, middlebrow cool choices like Sloane and Sutton. She compares using AI for baby names to online dating, saying a dating site might help you meet someone but you would not let it decide whether to marry them.

Redmond tells Axios that unlike AI chatbots, Nameberry can track what names people are searching for in real time, potentially spotting emerging trends before they show up in official government statistics. Nameberry's internal search data shows growing interest in names including Beatrice, Sabine, Fiona, Ivy, Mae, Marin, Gwendolyn, Murray and Conrad. Redmond is also watching Cassian, which she expects to become more popular because of the A Court of Thorns and Roses fantasy book series, and she suspects Rosemary, Mabel, Archie and Bodie will take off as well. The report closes by noting the irony that by sharing these names, it may have just given AI a few more to suggest.

stories.Headline: AI stocks in S&P 500 funds leave 401(k) holders facing volatility
stories.Summary:
The S&P 500 lost $5.6 trillion in market value during the week and closed more than 10% below the record high it set in early October, according to a report published on November 21, 2026. By the end of Friday's trading session, the AI stocks that make up a major part of the index had shown no sign of recovery. The report, carried by CNN and by ClickOrlando.com, tied the drop to the heavy presence of artificial intelligence companies in the index and in the retirement accounts that track it. It described the week as one in which the value of those holdings fell sharply and did not bounce back before trading ended.

The decline matters for people whose 401(k) plans hold funds that follow the S&P 500, because those accounts now carry a large share of AI-related stocks without the account holders necessarily choosing them. The report frames the situation as a question of how to deal with the volatility that comes with that exposure. It gives no specific figures for how much of a typical 401(k) sits in AI stocks and names no funds, plan providers or regulators. The only numbers it provides are the $5.6 trillion in lost market value, the more than 10% drop from the record high and the early October date of that high.

The articles do not name any official, company or spokesperson who is responsible for the decline or who commented on it, and they contain no statements from anyone about what account holders should do. Responsibility is described only in general terms, through the makeup of the index and the funds that track it. The report offers no quoted guidance from financial advisers, plan administrators or government agencies. It also does not say whether the losses are expected to continue or to reverse.

The context the articles give is limited to the market's recent record high in early October and the steep fall that followed in the week ending November 21, 2026. They do not say what happens next, whether the AI stocks will recover or whether 401(k) holders plan to change their investments. No follow-up reporting, regulatory action or company response is mentioned. The report leaves the outcome of the volatility open and provides no forecast for the coming weeks.

stories.Headline: Texas Sports Academy receives $6.5 million in state voucher funds
stories.Summary:
Texas Sports Academy, a sports academy connected to the artificial intelligence-driven Alpha School chain, had received $6.5 million in voucher dollars as of Oct. 30, according to the Texas Comptroller's online dashboard. The Texas Tribune reported the figure on Nov. 21, 2026, calling the academy the biggest recipient of Texas' new school voucher program so far. The academy calls itself an "elite sports academy built for serious student-athletes" and has several schools across the state in addition to a virtual campus. The disclosure comes a little more than a year after the State Board of Education voted 10-3 to reject Alpha leaders' bid to open a publicly funded charter school. The $6.5 million is more than twice the amount received by the second-largest recipient, San Antonio-based Cornerstone Christian Schools, which had gotten roughly $2.8 million.

The voucher program, formally called Texas Education Freedom Accounts, gives families public funds of roughly $10,500 to help pay for private school tuition and up to $2,000 for home-schooling expenses. The program also covers a wide range of approved educational expenses, like private tutoring and school supplies. Other top recipients included First Baptist Academy, which received almost $2 million, and Yeshiva Torat Emet, a Jewish school in Houston, which received nearly $1.6 million. The Christian School at Castle Hills received a little more than $1.5 million. The comptroller's dashboard shows Amazon was by far the largest private vendor, receiving $12.3 million, while the next largest, Rainbow Resource Center, Inc., received $2.3 million.

Outgoing Texas Comptroller Don Huffines said Friday his office is in the process of expanding the dashboard, according to a news release. Huffines said the expansion is intended to increase "insight into how TEFA funds are being used while maintaining protections for student and family privacy." The figures are public on the dashboard his office is expanding. Texas lawmakers, led by Gov. Greg Abbott, approved the voucher program in 2025. Alpha's rejection by the SBOE did not prevent it from participating in the voucher program, which allows families to receive state funding for use at private schools and for home schooling.

Board members raised concerns about the company's use of AI to teach, about students' screen time and about the large test-score gains Alpha leaders presented. As of September, the chain had roughly quadrupled its Texas private schools to more than 30 virtual and in-person campuses, and most were accepted into the voucher program, an investigation by The Texas Tribune and ProPublica found. Alpha's model has students complete core academics online in two hours a day using AI software, a tool the state's education commissioner, Mike Morath, and his agency have helped get into at least three public school districts this year. At Texas Sports Academy, an AI tutor "guides students through each lesson," according to the school's website. The setup, the website says, "leaves the rest of the day free for sports training, developing life skills, pursuing passions, and just being a kid."

After a couple hours of academics, the rest of the day is filled with various sports classes, such as soccer training, speed and agility training, and strength training, according to a sample student schedule. On Fridays at 3:30 p.m., an hour can be set aside for NBA watch parties. Texas Sports Academy is one of numerous institutions across the country connected to Alpha. Kindergarten and first grade students participated in a "putt-putt-palooza" workshop at the Alpha School campus in Austin on Sept. 9, 2025. Lexi Churchill contributed to the report.

The articles do not say what happens next beyond Huffines' statement that his office is expanding the dashboard. The articles leave open which other campuses most were accepted into the voucher program and how the expanded dashboard will look. The articles do not say whether Texas Sports Academy or Alpha responded to the figures. The articles do not give the total amount paid out under the program so far. The articles do not say when the dashboard expansion will be finished.

stories.Headline: Geoffrey Seiler identifies Alphabet, AMD and TSMC as potential winners if AI chips become commoditized
stories.Summary:
Geoffrey Seiler wrote that the AI chip market is shifting on November 21, 2026, which may weaken the grip of Nvidia. Anthropic recently revealed that its Claude Mythos model can run on alternative chips in a few days with almost no human intervention. This new process used to take dozens of engineers and six to 12 months to complete before this recent technical shift. Such a change reduces the CUDA moat of Nvidia while other competitors in the chip market are starting to catch up. This shift suggests that AI chips could become commoditized, which would be very bad news for the current market leader.

Commoditization would erode pricing power and shrink margins for Nvidia, whose gross margins are currently in the mid-70 percent range. Advanced Micro Devices has gross margins in the mid-50 percent range and offers the new Helios AI rack system. Alphabet uses Tensor Processing Units, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing provides manufacturing and packaging capacity for various chip designers and hyperscalers. Other mentioned companies include Broadcom, Marvell Technology, and SpaceX, the only large customer not developing its own custom AI chips. These changes affect the market for high bandwidth memory and the overall demand for various AI accelerators and custom ASICs.

Geoffrey Seiler stated that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing is a buy because it wins regardless of which specific AI chip customers choose. He noted that Alphabet is well positioned to benefit from commoditization because it has a decade head start with custom chips. Seiler argued that Alphabet can gain share with external customers without sacrificing margins because its offerings cost much less than Nvidia. He described Advanced Micro Devices as a buy because pricing normalization and chip fungibility act as a tailwind for the company. He believes the Helios system gives the company a big opportunity to be a meaningful alternative to Nvidia in coming years.

Semianalysis reported that Alphabet Tensor Processing Units have started to outperform Nvidia GPUs on a performance per dollar basis, though some dispute this. Customers are increasingly affected by cost per action and care more about CPU integrations and memory capacity for inference and agentic AI. Hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprises, and governments are the primary buyers of these chips, often sourcing them through Broadcom or Marvell Technology. Nvidia's largest customers are trying to break free from high prices by developing their own custom chips to reduce their dependency. These customers seek alternatives to the high premiums currently commanded by the hardware, software, and networking ecosystem created by Nvidia.

Nvidia previously appeared on a Motley Fool list on April 15, 2005, and a thousand dollar investment then would be worth 896,981 dollars. Netflix was recommended on December 17, 2004, and a thousand dollar investment would have grown to 315,271 dollars by November 2026. The Stock Advisor team reports a total average return of 768 percent compared to 198 percent for the S&P 500 index. Nvidia currently maintains advantages through its cohesive ecosystem and locked up access to constrained supplies of high bandwidth memory. The company also holds more manufacturing capacity with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing than its competitors do at this current point in time.

Nvidia will likely face continued pricing pressure and market share loss as the gap between different AI chips continues to shrink. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing may see lower customer concentration and improved gross margins if more alternatives to Nvidia GPUs become available. Alphabet will continue creating an ecosystem to rival chipmakers and improve the utilization of its own massive data center holdings. Advanced Micro Devices will attempt to establish itself as a primary alternative by leveraging its larger memory capacity for AI inference. The articles leave open whether Nvidia can maintain its premium pricing despite the rise of custom chips and competing GPU architectures.

stories.Headline: Nvidia beats revenue and earnings estimates amid surging AI demand
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA Corp. announced its financial results for the fiscal third quarter on November 22, 2026, showing a massive increase in demand for artificial intelligence. The company reported that its total revenue reached 115.84 billion dollars, which was significantly higher than the 109.08 billion dollars that analysts had estimated. Adjusted earnings for the period came in at 2.68 dollars per share, beating the expected amount of 2.48 dollars per share. This specific financial report was the first one released since founder and former chief executive officer Jensen Huang stepped down from his role last week.

The strong financial performance requires investors to consider the broader impact of artificial intelligence demand on the current market. These results highlight a period of acceleration for the company despite the recent leadership change at the top of the organization. The report confirms that the company is exceeding expectations in key areas while navigating a complex global economic environment. Every number provided in the report suggests that the company is maintaining a dominant position in the high tech hardware sector.

The data provided by Benzinga Pro was responsible for confirming that the revenue and earnings figures surpassed the forecasts of market analysts. While the company did not provide a direct statement, the reports indicate that the demand for AI technology is driving this growth. Other political figures have commented on the broader industry, such as Chuck Schumer who criticized the approval of AI chip sales to China. Schumer claimed that approving nearly 880,000 chip exports to Chinese firms created national security risks and benefited individuals over the country.

The context of this announcement involves a wider earnings season where companies are highlighting risks like rising investment costs and U.S. chip restrictions. Investors are currently weighing the growth of cloud computing and cybersecurity spending alongside these blockbuster results from the hardware sector. The market continues to monitor how leadership transitions and international trade policies will affect the long term trajectory of AI development. Future reports will likely focus on whether this acceleration can be sustained amidst increasing regulatory pressure from the United States government.

stories.Headline: Investors sell AI stocks as S&P 500 falls 12 percent from October high
stories.Summary:
The S&P 500 index slumped during the third quarter earnings season ending in November 2026. Investors sold off artificial intelligence stocks despite strong corporate profits. This market decline occurred between October and November. The index entered correction territory on Friday, November 21. This downturn followed the shock ouster of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang.

The S&P 500 fell 8.1 percent from JPMorgan results in October to Walmart's report on Thursday. It dropped another 3.7 percent Friday, falling 12 percent from its October 6 high. Democratic midterm wins raised fears of tighter data center regulation in the US. S&P 500 firms saw profit growth over 30 percent for two consecutive quarters. Dividends and buybacks fell to 53 percent of earnings, the lowest since 1990.

Daniel Farley of US Bank Wealth Management said the market will struggle as earnings growth rates slow. Marta Norton from Empower noted that the ability to monetize AI investments remains far off. Chris Grisanti of Mai Wealth Advisors said investors feel burned and wary of committing. Gina Martin Adams of HB Wealth Management called the synchronous earnings growth fleeting. Richard Flynn of Charles Schwab UK called Europe a compelling addition for diversification.

Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon slumped after reporting negative free cash flow in the third quarter. BofA Securities reported that fund managers cut tech exposure to the lowest level since 2006. Ford and General Motors slipped as analysts raised concerns about the 2027 outlook. Homebuilders DR Horton and NVR dropped after missing expectations for the quarter. Energy stocks rose 36 percent due to high prices from the Iran war.

The S&P 500 recorded earnings increases across all 11 sectors for the first time since 2021. Healthcare firms like UnitedHealth Group reported lower costs in the third quarter. Americans bought one million more turkeys for Thanksgiving than they did in 2025. European profits at MSCI constituents jumped 33 percent in the third quarter. The Stoxx 600 reached an all-time peak by mid-November.

Analysts lowered fourth quarter expectations at the fastest rate this year during early November. Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, and Ned Davis Research cited decelerating earnings through 2027 as a risk. Ed Clissold predicted the S&P 500 would only reach 8,000 by 2027. Ohsung Kwon set a slightly higher 2027 target of 8,200 for the index. The articles leave open whether Nvidia can recover from the cloud of Huang's ouster.

stories.Headline: London builds an AI safety hub as government funds model testing
stories.Summary:
London has established itself as a global center for artificial intelligence safety to ensure powerful models benefit society rather than cause harm. A growing ecosystem of researchers, policymakers, and campaigners in the capital is working to prevent these systems from causing damage. This effort involves various organizations focusing on risks like cyber misuse and the potential for models to lie or cheat. The city is now increasingly described as the leading hub for AI safety within the European region. These activities have intensified as warnings regarding the potential dangers of advanced technology continue to ramp up globally.

The government announced hundreds of millions of pounds for security, including 120 million pounds specifically for the AI Security Institute. This state-backed organization assesses leading models before and after release, while the London Initiative for Safe AI moves to King's Cross. Google DeepMind and Anthropic maintain major bases in London, where the London AI Hub counts up to 50 safety organizations. Basecamp Research operates from a former watch factory in Farringdon to help develop antibiotics and vaccines against future pandemics. The government will also launch an AI Biosecurity Lab to address threats from the development of harmful pathogens.

Rupert Elston of the London AI Hub says the city acts as a referee with clearly defined boundaries for talent. Oliver Vince of Basecamp Research believes London is a key player due to its unique opportunity, culture, history, and expertise. Professor Hannah Fry says the UK punches above its weight and focuses on ethical technology for good rather than hyper-capitalism. A spokesperson for Lord Khan stated that London has the talent and businesses needed to lead the way in AI. Hugh Brady of Imperial College London says AI is now embedded in education, research, and many local start-ups.

Gina Neff warns that researchers struggle to gain access to cutting-edge AI models before they are released to the general public. She argues that a few people in northern California should not set the terms of the future for everyone. Data centers face critical energy constraints, as noted in a report commissioned by the Greater London Authority for the capital. Imperial College London has over 750 people working on large language models or their various applications to help society. Activist Joseph Miller and his group, Pause AI UK, call for a halt to the development of frontier AI models.

London's role in AI safety grew from historical links to effective altruism and the presence of large student communities. Joseph Miller began this movement in 2021 by staging a protest outside the offices of Google DeepMind with a friend. The city has a track record of using regulatory sandboxes to test emerging technologies in controlled environments before wider deployment. The Telehouse data center in Canary Wharf uses a closed loop water system to manage its operational needs. These combined factors have helped the capital become a center for the intersection of AI and life science.

Pause AI UK held a protest in February with 300 people and plans a larger demonstration for this coming Saturday. The London AI and Jobs Taskforce will examine how AI changes work and how Londoners can prepare for those changes. Hugh Brady warns that AI in the wrong hands could harm the food chain, the environment, or the water supply. Researchers continue to work with OpenAI and Anthropic to get ahead of emerging threats and discover new medicines. The articles leave open whether these local efforts will genuinely make a difference on the global stage over time.

stories.Headline: HEARTBOT AI wins Chunghwa Telecom Special Award for its AI governance platform
stories.Summary:
HEARTBOT AI won the Chunghwa Telecom Special Award at Meet Neo Star 2026 during the Meet Taipei Startup Festival. CEO Nathan Yen pitched the AnyInsight platform at the Demo Show Final on November 20 to show judges AI control. The company was named to the top 30 from more than 200 startups for its zero-trust approach to governance. This event took place in Taipei, and the official announcement of the award was released on November 22, 2026. The competition was part of a larger festival that highlighted innovative startups and their security solutions for enterprise AI.

The prize from Chunghwa Telecom includes hicloud credits and priority eligibility for the final selection of CHT 5G Accelerator Batch 9. It also provides opportunities to collaborate with CHT business units, while Meet Taipei ran from November 19 to 21, 2026. The festival occurred at Taipei Expo Park and drew over 550 startups from 23 countries, making it the largest edition. AnyInsight uses over 20 cloud models, 350 ready-to-use agents, and 500 application connectors to build automated workflows in one environment. The platform is certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and follows the General Data Protection Regulation and the EU AI Act principles.

CEO Nathan Yen stated that companies no longer ask if they should use AI but worry about tracking agent actions. He explained that AnyInsight provides every interaction with an owner and a record, allowing AI to enter core operations. Yen noted that recognition from the Meet Neo Star judges is very meaningful for a startup focused on AI governance. He added that many companies now view control as a necessary condition for adopting AI in their daily business. The CEO believes that providing visibility into data usage is the primary problem his company works on every day.

Many employees use personal AI accounts for work, which leaves no company record and creates gaps in corporate oversight. Individual teams often build agents that run without IT knowledge, sometimes continuing long after the original creators have left. Auditors frequently find that teams must spend several weeks pulling together AI usage records by hand to meet requirements. Taiwanese companies operating internationally are affected by Article 50 of the EU AI Act, which began applying in August 2026. These regulations add pressure on businesses to make AI governance a part of their day to day operations.

The company previously received the ASOCIO Global Business Service Award in October and announced AnyInsight Edge on November 12, 2026. Edge extends governance to on-premises servers and data centers as a container that does not require a GPU. This solves problems for companies bound by data residency rules that have private models stuck as simple internal chatbots. These private models often lack access to core systems like CRM, ERP, and MES without the new Edge control plane. The system supports on-premises models such as Mistral and Gemma while keeping all conversations and audit logs in-house.

AnyInsight uses a generative AI firewall with semantic analysis to block or mask personal, financial, health data, and cloud credentials. It checks policy and authorizes access by role using the Model Context Protocol before an agent calls a tool. High-risk actions require human approval, and every event is logged as exportable evidence to help organizations pass compliance audits. The articles do not state when the CHT 5G Accelerator Batch 9 selection will occur or the specific credit amounts. They also leave open how many companies have already deployed the Edge version in their own private data centers.

stories.Headline: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes industry-wide development limits tied to perplexity
stories.Summary:
OpenAI called on frontier AI developers to adopt common limits on model development tied partly to perplexity, in a post published on Sunday, November 22, 2026, by Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki. He proposed an industry standard that would set measurable thresholds developers agree not to cross until matching advances are made in understanding and monitoring AI behavior. Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token, with lower readings meaning better performance, and OpenAI generally tracks its logarithm, also called cross-entropy loss. Pachocki argued the measure has stayed unusually useful for tracking the underlying intelligence created during pretraining even as downstream AI benchmarks quickly become obsolete.

OpenAI said GPT-3.5 registered log-perplexity of about 0.99 on its main internal evaluation dataset, while GPT-4 reached about 0.91. As losses moved below 0.8, the company began seeing transformative capabilities in areas including cybersecurity and mathematics, and a model at roughly 0.76 began producing what Pachocki described as groundbreaking mathematical results. He said OpenAI expects further transformative capabilities as models move into roughly the 0.68 to 0.70 range, although the company does not know what those capabilities will be. That uncertainty underpins the proposed limits, under which frontier labs would agree on shared evaluation and red-teaming standards and set a first threshold they would not cross until monitoring technology reached a defined milestone, such as a successor to current chain-of-thought monitoring systems.

Pachocki is responsible for the proposal, and he argued that greater transparency around the measure could give the industry a shared scientific basis for pacing increasingly capable AI systems. OpenAI acknowledged that perplexity is an imperfect common standard, because results can be difficult to compare between laboratories that use different datasets and training mixtures, and because the metric does not capture all capability gains, including those produced by chain-of-thought reasoning. The proposal comes as OpenAI sees AI beginning to contribute to its own development, and Pachocki said an acceleration in pretraining research could emerge as soon as 2027 if AI systems begin generating fundamental algorithmic advances. That could speed progress faster than alignment and monitoring techniques can keep pace, which is the concern the proposed development limits are meant to address.
