stories.Headline: Gemini 3.0 Pro matches expert algorithms on cancer symptom guidance but falls short on depression
stories.Summary:
A multicenter research team from the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Northeastern University, Elimu Informatics, Brigham and Women's Hospital, and the Medical University of South Carolina tested Google DeepMind's Gemini 3.0 Pro on two clinical informatics functions. The team evaluated the model's ability to interpret narrative and semi-structured updates in published clinical guidelines and incorporate them into existing symptom management algorithms. The team also assessed the model's ability to translate complex decision trees into patient-specific clinical recommendations for simulated patient vignettes. The study was published in Frontiers in Medicine and covered cancer-related fatigue, pain, and depression. The artificial intelligence system demonstrated high concordance with expert consensus standards and rule-based decision support logic.

The study evaluated decision support algorithms from the Sapphire Cancer Symptom Management system, known as CDS-Sx, which classify clinical knowledge across four operational layers. The original fatigue algorithm comprised 29 decision nodes and 19 unique clinical pathways. The depression algorithm spanned 42 decision nodes and 39 pathways. The pain algorithm encompassed 1,425 decision nodes and 3,194 separate pathways. The authors supplied Gemini 3.0 Pro with explicit Level 2 semi-structured decision trees alongside formal guideline documents.

Two-member expert review panels used an agile rapid qualitative analysis methodology combined with evidence mapping. The panels scored each proposed algorithmic update across four predefined rubric domains. Detection was scored on a zero-to-two scale, completeness on a zero-to-three scale, accuracy on a zero-to-three scale, and safety risk on a zero-to-two scale. Pre-specified acceptable study-level performance required a mean detection score of at least 1.5, mean completeness of at least 2.0, and mean accuracy of at least 2.0. At least 80 percent of items had to meet acceptable individual thresholds and at least 95 percent had to introduce no meaningful clinical risk.

For cancer-related fatigue, the model exceeded all pre-specified acceptability thresholds across 19 evaluated items. It recorded a mean detection score of 1.9, a mean completeness score of 2.8, a mean accuracy score of 2.8, and a safety score of 2.0, with 100 percent of items deemed free of clinical risk. The system elevated evidence-based non-pharmacologic interventions such as exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy, and mindfulness to first-line status while discouraging routine psychostimulant use. The model incorporated critical opioid safety measures, identified contraindications for meperidine, and highlighted pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions between dexamethasone and opioids metabolized by CYP3A4. It confirmed transdermal buprenorphine as a valuable therapy in patients presenting with renal impairment.

For depression, mean detection reached 1.0, completeness averaged 1.6, and accuracy averaged 1.5, with only 57 percent of items meeting acceptable accuracy criteria. This decline was driven by the omission of non-pharmacologic integrative modalities from Society for Integrative Oncology companion guidelines, including music therapy, reflexology, relaxation techniques, Tai Chi, and Qi Gong. The model generated explicit agent-level suggestions, such as favoring specific selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or avoiding paroxetine in patients taking tamoxifen due to CYP2D6 inhibition. Clinician judges noted that the suggestions were safe, clinically appropriate, and concordant with practice.

The model maintained an uncompromised safety profile. The first vignette described a 62-year-old man with stage IV small cell lung cancer, bone metastases, stage 3b chronic kidney disease, and severe persistent fatigue. The second vignette detailed a 55-year-old woman with metastatic colon cancer receiving FOLFIRI chemotherapy who presented with severe depression, moderate abdominal pain, and chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy. The third vignette involved a 55-year-old man with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer invading the brachial plexus who experienced severe mixed somatic and neuropathic pain despite escalating sustained-release and immediate-release morphine regimens.

Across all three vignettes, the model registered overall F1-scores between 0.86 and 0.96 and a precision score of 1.00 in all three cases. For the fatigue vignette, the system achieved a recall between 0.86 and 0.92, reproducing 12 of 14 reference recommendations and omitting only late-line integrative therapies and short-course dexamethasone intended primarily for end-of-life care. In the depression vignette, the model achieved a recall of 0.85 by reproducing 11 of 13 recommendations, correctly suggesting mental health referral, duloxetine initiation to address co-occurring neuropathy, physical therapy, and bowel prophylaxis, while omitting oral non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and naloxone co-prescription. In the pain vignette, the model produced an F1-score of 0.86 and a recall of 0.75, generating 9 of 12 reference recommendations.

The system correctly guided opioid titration, recommended topical lidocaine patches for focal neuropathic burning, initiated gabapentin titration, incorporated cold and heat therapy, recommended bone-modifying agents, and added naloxone co-prescription and bowel prophylaxis. The three missing elements were scheduled acetaminophen, upward duloxetine titration, and future consideration of a tricyclic antidepressant if initial therapies failed. Qualitative analysis confirmed that discordance stemmed entirely from omission rather than commission. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Gene Munster attributes AI stock sell-off to investor fear rather than fundamentals
stories.Summary:
Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management reported on Friday, November 21, 2026, that a recent sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks is driven by investor fear. Several companies focused on this technology have seen their values drop between 30% and 50% over the last six weeks. The Nasdaq index has declined by roughly 16% since the beginning of October, though this is not an unprecedented event. This downturn is fueled by anxiety regarding future earnings, financing conditions, and the sustainability of data center construction.

The current market situation requires more buyers than sellers to end the decline and stabilize prices. Investors are specifically worried about potential estimate cuts over multiple quarters and the impact of export restrictions related to China. Other critical factors include political resistance to new data centers and the ongoing role of Nvidia in supporting the ecosystem. Munster noted that the market previously experienced a 24% sell-off during the DeepSeek shock and tariff uncertainty in early 2025.

Munster stated that the sell-off is about psychology rather than deteriorating fundamentals, though he admitted that getting the fundamentals right does not always mean getting the stock price right. He suggested that late January could be a turning point when companies report their December-quarter results. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives also argued that the downturn is disconnected from reality and that the AI opportunity is less than 15% complete. Ives believes that chip demand remains robust and that this period represents a generational opportunity to buy winning companies.

stories.Headline: Bytedance releases an open model to show that AI training pipelines can be simplified
stories.Summary:
A team from the parent company of TikTok, Bytedance, and several universities in the United States released a new paper on November 21, 2026. These researchers argue that the complex training pipelines currently used for AI agents are largely unnecessary for achieving high performance. They aim to prove that only three specific training steps are required to create a competitive open model. This effort challenges the current industry trend of stacking numerous nested training phases one after another.

The proposed approach simplifies how models learn to research the web, run code, and solve multi-step tasks. By reducing the number of phases, the team believes it will be easier to identify which specific steps actually improve the model. This change addresses the growing problem where reproducing AI work has become prohibitively expensive for many developers. The researchers suggest that the current method of layering training stages makes it nearly impossible to track effectiveness.

The Bytedance team is responsible for these findings and believes that the industry has overcomplicated the development of AI agents. They state that the current reliance on deeply nested pipelines creates unnecessary barriers to innovation and transparency. By providing a competitive open model, they intend to demonstrate that a streamlined process can yield similar results. This move encourages other developers to move away from expensive and opaque training methodologies.

stories.Headline: Human auditors fully identify only 17 percent of planted sabotage mechanisms in a Redwood Research study
stories.Summary:
Human auditors fully identified only 17 percent of the sabotage mechanisms planted in a Redwood Research study, the Superpower Daily Editorial Desk reported on November 21, 2026. The experiment covered 22 research logs, 10 benign and 12 sabotaged, containing 33 distinct mechanisms. Twenty-five auditors completed 104 reviews, each with a 90-minute time limit. Their ability to distinguish sabotaged work from honest work was barely above chance, and the difference was not statistically significant. They missed 74 percent of mechanisms entirely.

Keshav Shenoy and seven coauthors submitted the paper to arXiv on November 16 and revised it November 18, and their November 20 Redwood Research post details the methods and caveats. One researcher produced the 22 full research logs, and the altered runs contained 33 distinct sabotage mechanisms, 17 of them classified as major. Auditors received the complete log, AI-generated audits, access to frontier models and unlimited computing resources, and they assigned a probability that sabotage had occurred and offered five guesses about its mechanism. Their discrimination score was 0.59 on AUROC, not statistically better than chance, and no decision threshold caught most sabotaged runs without also flagging many benign ones. In one log, four of five auditors found one major mechanism, but nobody found the other two.

The authors describe potential sabotage ranging from subtle bugs and poor methods to omitted results and unsupported conclusions. Awarding half credit for partially identifying a mechanism, humans scored 21.9 percent, compared with 37.1 percent for Claude Fable 5.1 and 32.6 percent for GPT-6 Astra, while weaker models scored near or below the human auditors. Astra and Fable also scored higher than humans at distinguishing sabotaged logs, with AUROCs of 0.74 and 0.73, but those advantages were not statistically significant. The authors describe stronger models as likely outperforming humans rather than establishing a clear winner. Combining every human and AI audit still left 13 of the 33 mechanisms never fully identified.

After each sabotaged experiment, the saboteur rated its likely detectability, and restricting analysis to attacks rated harder to catch reduced mechanism identification, reaching zero for the two hardest-rated attacks, though overall ability to distinguish sabotaged from benign research did not fall. The saboteur knew the honest experimental results before designing attacks, and asked to predict those results, Redwood researchers fully predicted only about 40 percent of outcomes. The authors say this suggests targeted sabotage may be harder than their setup implies. All logs came from one researcher, the statistical uncertainty was wide, and projects were small, with the largest taking two weeks of serial work. Auditors had less AI safety experience than the authors would want in real-world reviews.

The experiment tested a potential defense against future AI misconduct, not sabotage carried out by an autonomous AI. The central test was whether auditors could distinguish honest research from work a human expert had deliberately steered toward a substantially different conclusion. The researchers also tested nine AI models, none allowed to run experiments. The authors see potential in AI auditors that can review research histories repeatedly at a scale too costly for expert humans. But using audit findings to train away sabotage creates another problem: false accusations could penalize legitimate research, degrading capabilities or making training less efficient.

The authors note that catching more suspicious work is not the same as knowing what to correct. The study signals a difficult oversight problem without establishing how audits would perform in real-world research. The small study leaves substantial uncertainty, and the saboteur had advance knowledge of results. The benchmark used small projects from one researcher. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Human auditors miss most planted sabotage in AI safety research study

stories.Headline: Capgemini's cash flows support an intrinsic value above its €117.70 share price
stories.Summary:
Capgemini's share price has drifted lower in recent years, and on 21 November 2026 Simply Wall St published an article asking whether the current €117.70 level still lines up with what its cash flows can support over time. The article was written by Bailey Pemberton and appeared on finance.yahoo.com at 06:00 UTC. It says recent headlines around AI, automation and supply chain resilience keep the story in focus. It says those headlines do not answer how the stock lines up against its own intrinsic value. Over the past 5 years the share price has fallen 34.7%.

The article says the question is whether expectations for Capgemini's future cash generation have also reset or whether the market has moved more than the underlying business. It says Capgemini's positioning in connected manufacturing, autonomous AI and supply chain resilience, including activity through its venture fund, can influence how investors think about the durability and timing of future cash flows. It cites a 14.5x P/E and points readers to a Discounted Cash Flow view. It says the group has produced roughly €2.17b in free cash flow over the last twelve months. It says analysts expect free cash flow to stay in the billions with a growing profile over the coming decade rather than a one off spike.

The article says the projections suggest these future cash flows support an intrinsic value substantially above the current €117.70 share price. It says Capgemini is being recognised in manufacturing services for areas like connected plants and AI driven operations. It says recent news helps explain why investors may be starting to reassess how durable those projected cash flows could be over a long horizon. It says Simply Wall St Narratives spell out which assumptions about future growth, margins and earnings would need to hold for the stock to be worth meaningfully more or less than today's share price. It says each narrative lays out the moving parts behind its fair value view so readers can later compare those inputs with actual results as they are reported.

The article says Capgemini's story splits into two readings, with one side seeing the AI and free cash flow plan underpriced and the other focused on restructuring and debt risk. It describes a bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St that focuses on Capgemini's AI initiatives and planned free cash flow profile. That Narrative says Capgemini is treating agentic AI as a full enterprise redesign rather than a single tool rollout, which could support higher value consulting, modernization and control plane projects. The article says this Narrative puts Capgemini at 34% undervalued. It describes a bearish analyst Narrative that emphasizes restructuring charges, leverage and contract risk rather than the potential AI upside.

The bearish Narrative says the Fit for Growth program involves €700m of restructuring costs over 2026 and 2027 with a heavy concentration in 2026. It says that if the resizing of weaker regions such as France does not quickly lift utilization, the combination of underused staff and elevated restructuring and financing expenses could suppress reported EPS and organic free cash flow versus current expectations. The article says this Narrative puts Capgemini at 10% overvalued. It says price, cash flow and AI plans only tell part of the story, because the people setting priorities and how they are rewarded can tilt outcomes in very different directions. It directs readers to see who runs Capgemini and how they are paid.

stories.Headline: Researchers find elderly health monitoring AI lacks human centered privacy features
stories.Summary:
An international research team published a comprehensive review in Discover Artificial Intelligence on November 21, 2026. They found that health monitoring AI for the elderly rarely uses human centered privacy features. The researchers examined how algorithmic safeguards align with human centered artificial intelligence dimensions. They discovered that most systems rely on technical data transformations rather than user controls. These systems often fail to involve elderly end users directly in the design process.

The team analyzed forty-five primary studies published between 2020 and 2025 from IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and Web of Science. They retrieved 202 initial records during search cycles in May 2025 and May 2026. Research was concentrated in Asia, with India providing eight studies, China six, and Japan five. The United States and Taiwan contributed three each, while Australia and Canada provided two each. Fourteen other nations and two multi-country partnerships also contributed to the reviewed literature.

The authors stated that nominal transparency is not meaningful human oversight if elderly users cannot comprehend the feedback. They noted that technical explainability must become actionable, low-burden indicators to protect vulnerable populations. The researchers argued that most studies rely on inferred alignment rather than explicit human relevant considerations. They found that ethical awareness is often reduced to mathematical data perturbation or privacy-by-design engineering. The team highlighted that personal autonomy and patient dignity remain largely unexamined in the literature.

Older adults are affected by cognitive, accessibility, and digital literacy barriers when navigating complex privacy settings. Patients are vulnerable to risks from unprocessed audio, video feeds, thermopile arrays, wearable telemetry, and smart-home sensors. The review found that 85 percent of papers designed systems specifically for older populations. These users face threats from cybersecurity breaches and the use of untrusted third-party cloud infrastructure. Only four studies provided explicit documentation of human relevant considerations, but none evaluated them with elderly participants.

Remote health monitoring gathers sensitive physiological, behavioral, and environmental information to reduce frequent in-person medical examinations. Systems focus on Android-based Ambient Assisted Living, smart home care, nursing facility dementia monitoring, and gait analysis. Most models concentrate on prediction and detection tasks, specifically fall detection and activities of daily living. Technical approaches include federated learning, edge AI, and data minimization using LiDAR or millimeter-wave radar. International conferences accounted for 60 percent of the literature, while journals provided 34 percent and preprints 6 percent.

The researchers performed a sensitivity analysis showing that alignment with human values decreases when rigorous standards are enforced. Only one study addressed more than one human centered dimension simultaneously. Future work must address the psychological impact of persistent ambient surveillance on elderly patients. The articles leave open how to effectively translate technical explainability into user-facing controls for seniors. The study was limited to English-language literature, potentially omitting relevant research on responsible artificial intelligence.

stories.Headline: Graham Dumpleton builds Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for Python apps
stories.Summary:
Graham Dumpleton, who created mod_wsgi twenty years ago, has started a new project called Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for running Python web applications, and Simon Willison linked to it on 21st November 2026. Dumpleton has spent two decades thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web apps in production since he began mod_wsgi. Muru aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps in both development and production. As he did with an earlier project called wrapture, Dumpleton is publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the work as part of his development process.

The project is written in Rust and relies heavily on AI assistance, though Dumpleton says deciding what is not good enough yet remains his job. He credits twenty years of getting things wrong with mod_wsgi as useful experience for that judgment. He says he is prepared to put in the hard work to keep polishing Muru until it is something he would trust and something users would trust too. The articles give no release date, version number or availability details for Muru.

Dumpleton is the person responsible for the project, and his stated position is that the AI may do a lot of the work on the surface but the standard-setting stays with him. He frames the twenty years of mod_wsgi mistakes as an asset rather than a liability for judging the new server. He commits to continuing the polishing work until the server meets a bar he would trust himself. The articles do not say who else, if anyone, is involved in the project.

The context is that Muru follows the same open, detailed development write-up approach Dumpleton used for wrapture. Willison's link post appeared on 21st November 2026, and the article carries a timestamp of 22nd November 2026. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Dumpleton's stated intention to keep polishing Muru. No timeline, funding or adoption information is given.

stories.Headline: OpenAI requires prior approval for platforms that give third parties direct access to its models
stories.Summary:
OpenAI began requiring operators of platforms that give third parties direct access to its models to obtain the company's prior review and approval, under a rewritten version of its Usage Policies. The new text carries an effective date of November 20, 2026, and replaces the version that had applied since October 29, 2025. OpenAI announced the changes in a changelog entry dated October 21, 2026, which gave customers 30 days before the rules took hold. The rewrite also adds a section barring the use of OpenAI models and outputs to prepare training material for rival AI systems. The policy body grew from about 830 words in the October 2025 version to about 1,400 words in the new one, according to a PPC Land count of the two texts.

The policy states that operators of a model-access intermediary platform or other service enabling third parties to directly access OpenAI models must obtain prior review and approval. It states that this requirement does not apply solely because an application integrates OpenAI models to power its features or functionality. The rewrite rewrites the child safety rules and widens the human review rule from automated decisions to automated actions, with a definition covering actions, decisions, transactions, submissions, and other steps. Three headed sections are new: Training and developing models, OpenAI-approved use, and Providing access to our models. The training section states its restrictions do not prohibit uses expressly permitted by an applicable Agreement with OpenAI, including any Permitted Exception under the Services Agreement.

The changelog entry states that OpenAI updated its Usage Policies to clarify restrictions on using OpenAI models and outputs to train other models. It states that OpenAI also clarified protections for children and teens and requirements for high-stakes uses, and that the update incorporates existing national security principles and sets out approval requirements for national security and law enforcement uses, as well as for model-access intermediaries. A help center notice titled "We're updating our Usage Policies" lists the same four themes and describes the training language as a clarification of restrictions that already existed rather than a new prohibition. It describes the intermediary rule as an added approval requirement and states that existing agreements and other applicable terms, including any express permissions granted in them, continue to apply. Under the heading "OpenAI-approved use," the policy states that OpenAI may grant specific partners case-by-case exceptions to certain restrictions, naming the factors reviewed as the partner, proposed use, applicable safeguards, and the partner's compliance commitments.

Elena Gurevich, an AI and intellectual property attorney who advises companies on AI governance, wrote in a LinkedIn post on November 20 that OpenAI's updated usage policies kicked in that day. She summarized the intermediary rule as meaning that a business providing customers direct access to OpenAI's models needs OpenAI's approval first, while using the models to power an application's features does not trigger the requirement. She gave OpenRouter, which she described as a platform that streamlines access to multiple AI models from different providers, as an example of the kind of service in scope, and OpenAI's policy names no company. The changelog records that on October 25, 2022, developers no longer needed to wait for approval after submitting as long as they complied with the policies.

It records that on November 9, 2022, OpenAI no longer required developers to register their applications, using a combination of automated and manual methods to monitor for policy violations instead. In August, data drawn from OpenRouter showed AI agents using nearly five times as many tokens per task as human users, with agent usage up about 14 times since February 2026 and more than 85% of agent token spend going to cached prompts. When Anthropic's rewritten Usage Policy took effect on November 12, 2026, it added a prohibition on reselling, proxying or otherwise providing access to Claude through unauthorized means, naming services that route requests through consumer subscriptions or misrepresent which product or client is in use. The training section opens with a rationale stating that capable models must have safeguards proportionate to the risks they pose before they are deployed, and that training another model on OpenAI outputs can transfer capabilities without carrying those safeguards over.

The operative prohibition states that users must not use OpenAI models or their outputs to generate, prepare, select, or supply training material or signals for models intended as alternatives to or substitutes for OpenAI models or services. The policy lists what that covers, including creating or preparing training data, training tasks, rubrics, or reinforcement-learning environments, and providing feedback used in training, including labels, scores, rankings, preferences, rewards, or corrections. Neither the policy page nor the help notice describes how to apply, how long a review takes, whether services already running on November 20 have a transition window, or whether any intermediary has already been approved. The policy gives no application route, form or review time for the access rule.

OpenAI's documents do not state a rationale for the intermediary section. The introductory text remains unchanged word for word, including the statement that OpenAI reserves all rights to withhold access where it reasonably believes it necessary to protect its service or users or anyone else. The privacy section still bars uses such as facial recognition databases built without data subject consent and reads exactly as before. More to follow.

stories.Headline: EU consortium 2DFIRE develops graphene and barium titanate modulators for AI data center optics
stories.Summary:
A new European Union project called 2DFIRE has officially started with seven partners from five European countries, and the Universitat Politècnica de València in Spain coordinates the consortium. The other partners are Lumiphase from Switzerland, KU Leuven from Belgium, Graphenea from Spain, Annealsys from France, Riga Technical University from Latvia and PNO Innovation from Spain. The project has a total budget of €4.92 million, which is about US$5.4 million, and it will run for 36 months. The work is funded by the European Union under the Graphene Flagship. The project aims to develop faster, smaller and more energy-efficient photonic devices for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.

Its approach is a hybrid platform that combines barium titanate, a ferroelectric material, with two-dimensional materials such as graphene and MoS₂. The core target is electro-optic modulators for optical interconnects in data centers, and the consortium points to electricity use in AI data centers, which it expects to more than double by 2030. According to the project page, the devices are barium titanate coupled-modulated ring modulators, and the target is data transmission at 400 Gbps per wavelength. Besides graphene and MoS₂, the work covers hydrogen-doped indium oxide as a transparent conducting oxide. The aims include thermal phase shifting with low optical losses and new electrode designs that cut driving voltage and energy use.

The partners will work on reliable methods to deposit and transfer the two-dimensional materials and integrate them with barium titanate devices. The project also aims to show that the modulators are compatible with existing semiconductor manufacturing processes and value chains, including 200 mm wafer technology. The consortium says this compatibility should support industrial adoption and strengthen Europe's semiconductor and photonics supply chains. The articles do not name individual people or give direct statements beyond the consortium's published positions on the project page. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the 36-month work plan and the stated aims.

stories.Headline: AI spending concerns and high rates push Dow and Nasdaq sharply lower
stories.Summary:
The Dow Jones 30 and Nasdaq 100 dropped significantly last week as uncertainty in the Middle East, concerns about AI spending and high interest rates continued to pressure US stocks, according to FXEmpire analyst Muhammad Umair. The Dow Jones closed at 48,350.30, down 1.52%, and the S&P 500 closed at 6,954.55, down 3.09%, both on Nov 20 at 21:59 UTC. The US Tech 100 closed at 25,237.55, down 4.68%, on Nov 20 at 21:59 UTC. Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) lost 13.8% and closed at 125.53, down 14.01%, on Nov 20 at 20:59 UTC. Caterpillar Inc. (CAT) dropped 5% and closed at 510.45, down 5.01%, on Nov 20 at 20:59 UTC.

The Nasdaq 100 dropped 9.38% last week to close at 25,237.50 and broke key support at 26,200, which suggests a decline towards 23,500. A break below 23,500 may trigger a deeper decline to the 200-week SMA near 21,000, and the index must recover above 28,000 to initiate the next rally. The Dow Jones broke below key support at 50,000 last week and closed with a loss of 7.24%, which suggests a drop towards 45,000 if it remains below 50,000. A break below 45,000 may trigger a deeper correction towards 38,500, a break below 48,000 may continue momentum towards 45,000, and a break above 50,000 may open the way towards 55,000. The Fed minutes released on 18 November kept the risk of higher interest rates in the near future, and officials discussed the risk of AI spending and rapid growth of related debt.

President Donald Trump said the US is very close to agreement with Mexico after meeting Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum in Asia, and Sheinbaum said talks about vehicles, steel and aluminum have made progress. She mentioned that agreement can be made during the next meeting at the G20 summit in December. The White House mentioned that The Boeing Company (BA) and GE Aerospace have finalized a $12 billion sale to Philippine Airlines for up to 20 Boeing 787 aircraft with GE engines. Boeing (BA) traded at $157.09, down 1.09%, on Nov 21 at 09:44 UTC. Umair wrote that confirmed relief in tariffs may provide clear benefits to industrial sectors of the Dow.

The final University of Michigan survey released on Friday showed consumer sentiment increased to 51.5 in November from 48.0 in October. One-year inflation expectations dropped to 3.7% from 4.7% while long-term expectations eased to 3.3% from 3.5%. Initial jobless claims increased by 1000 to 203,000 and continued claims increased by 70,000 to 1.763 million for the first week of November. The 10-year US Treasury yield dropped to 4.91% on Friday after a strong spike to 5.17% following US consumer inflation data, and the 10-year yield lies at 0.96% above the three-month bill rate.

WTI crude oil closed at 84.9520, up 0.94%, and gold (XAU) closed at 3,538.19, down 1.92%, both on Nov 20 at 21:59 UTC. The weekly Nasdaq 100 chart shows a cup and handle formation from November 2021 to November 2023, and the RSI is approaching oversold levels as the index drops towards 23,500. The daily chart shows a broadening wedge pattern from June 2026, and the index broke the 200-day SMA at 28,000 and dropped 4.63% on Friday. The Dow Jones long-term support at 38,500 is defined by an ascending broadening wedge pattern from January 2024, and 45,000 represents the neckline of an inverted head and shoulders pattern formed from December 2024 to August 2025.

Iran may make the US blockade of Iranian ports as difficult as possible with the hope that the US will withdraw, and shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz are shrinking. The recent selloff in WTI oil, gold and US stocks may be the symptom of shrinking liquidity. Umair wrote that the Nasdaq 100 and Dow Jones remain under extreme pressure in the short term and that a lasting recovery needs strong confidence in corporate profits and returns from AI investment. He wrote that concerns about profitability from AI spending outweigh the benefits of cheaper long-term funding.

The articles leave open whether the US-Mexico agreement will be announced and whether the Fed will raise rates in December. The articles do not state whether the 23,500 support for the Nasdaq 100 or the 45,000 support for the Dow Jones will hold. The articles do not give the outcome of the next meeting at the G20 summit in December. The articles do not state when the US blockade of Iranian ports began or how far shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz have shrunk.

stories.Headline: Fujitsu and FamilyMart pilot causal AI to analyze purchases of decarbonized innerwear
stories.Summary:
Fujitsu Limited announced on November 22, 2026, that it has launched a pilot study with FamilyMart Co., Ltd. to analyze consumer purchasing behavior and establish a demand creation model for decarbonized products. The study combines Fujitsu Causal AI, a core technology of the Fujitsu Kozuchi AI platform, with LLM causal technology. The initiative is part of the Model Project for Creating Demand for Decarbonized Products, a program publicly solicited by Japan's Ministry of the Environment. The two companies will focus the pilot on environmentally friendly innerwear sold by FamilyMart.

The study will analyze sales data and survey results collected through FamilyMart's Famipay app to clarify how information and consumer touchpoints help customers understand a product's environmental value and lead to a purchase. The companies will then implement in-store initiatives to verify their effectiveness and aim to establish a robust demand creation model. The insights and analytical methods gained are expected to be applied to other categories beyond apparel, including food, daily necessities, and household goods. The Ministry of the Environment's model project aims to promote investment and innovation in decarbonization and to encourage consumer selection of these products, thereby fostering market formation.

The featured items are made with recycled polyester fibers that reduce CO2 emissions compared with conventional synthetic fibers, by 15% for inner T-shirts and 8% for REHEAT products. The Ministry of the Environment describes the project as one that appropriately displays the decarbonization value of products and services and develops an environment where consumers and procurement entities can understand and evaluate such value, assessing tolerance for price premiums and impacts on purchasing behavior. LLM causal technology is described as a technology that discovers intervention points by having an LLM complement intermediate factors not present in the quantitative data, based on causal relationships estimated from the data. Fujitsu reported consolidated revenues of 3.5 trillion yen, or US$23 billion, for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.

The companies will continue to discuss methods for effectively communicating environmental value and optimizing retail environments, and they will explore applying Fujitsu Causal AI to other product categories. By doing so, the partners aim to contribute to the creation of demand for decarbonized products and enhance customer value in the retail sector through advanced, data-driven marketing. Fujitsu states that its purpose is to make the world more sustainable by building trust in society through innovation, with 100,000 employees working to resolve challenges facing humanity.

stories.Headline: Hitachi Digital launches HARC Compose to govern agentic AI engineering
stories.Summary:
Hitachi Digital Inc. launched HARC Compose on November 18, 2026, in Santa Clara, California, according to a release dated November 22, 2026. Hitachi Digital is the global digital services company recently unveiled by Hitachi, Ltd. The product combines technology and services to govern the lifecycle of agentic engineering across complex, AI-driven systems. It does so through enterprise specific context, guardrails and intent. The release says it helps companies orchestrate AI from development to deployment through to operations and continuous improvement in a closed loop.

HARC Compose builds on Hitachi's experience and uses standardized, failure-conscious engineering. Hitachi Digital FDEs, forward deployed engineers, use it to build trustworthy AI-native applications faster and to maintain and improve AI agent performance once deployed. It strengthens Hitachi Digital's recurring service model, giving FDEs end-to-end support from ideas to outcomes. It is compatible across multi-vendor environments, and enterprises can use it entirely or opt for individual capabilities. It strengthens HMAX by Hitachi and augments HMAX Foundry solutions including HMAX Data Fabric, HMAX AI Operations, and HMAX Cyber.

Hitachi Digital is the unified brand of GlobalLogic, Inc. and Hitachi Digital Services LLC, and its legal entity is scheduled to be established on April 1, 2027. A press release on September 3, 2026 covered Hitachi expanding HMAX to accelerate deployment of Physical AI. Anand Birje, CEO and Chairman of Hitachi Digital, said HARC Compose is Hitachi Digital in action. He said the true promise of AI is not just writing code faster but shifting human ingenuity toward composing resilient, mission-critical systems. He said eliminating the divide between build and run closes the feedback loop and delivers governance and trust.

Premkumar Balasubramanian, Chief Technology Officer of Hitachi Digital, said speed is expected and trust has to be earned in an era of AI-generated software. He said customers need clarity on what a change is meant to improve, proof that it worked, and confidence in the process behind it. He said forward deployed engineers direct AI agents to build, test, and coordinate changes while maintaining strict human oversight over what goes live. He said live production evidence verifies outcomes. The release says AI has made code development faster and more productive but not necessarily trustworthy across enterprise systems.

The release says that without the right context, enterprise knowledge, company goals, policies, systems, and risk requirements, fast code becomes fast failure. HARC Compose carries enterprise intent from planning through production while keeping human experts in control of critical decisions. It includes CAKE, the Context-Aware Knowledge Engine, which connects enterprise intent, domain knowledge, systems, policies, risks, security, decision and production history and flags gaps and contradictions before agents act. An Orchestration Engine coordinates multiple agents across build, deploy and operate as one system and supports various AI agents and tools selected by customers. Failure-conscious Engineering uses failure mode and effects analysis to identify how a proposed change could fail and to decide what to test before release.

Universal capabilities include Responsible AI, which guards against system deviations such as agent drift, and guided and autonomous work that maintain human engagement. HARC Compose is built on OFE, outcome-forward engineering, a methodology used by Hitachi Digital's own FDE teams, which treats Define, Build, Deploy and Operate as one continuous system. Delivery is considered complete only when a system yields intended business outcomes in the real world, not at system release. The release lists principles including Fidelity, which establishes intent, constraints, failure risks and guardrails before work begins, and Throughput, which uses coding agents to turn clear intent into operable change. HARC Compose is available to enterprises worldwide, and deployments supported by Hitachi Digital FDEs are already underway in the finance, healthcare, and technology industries.

Hitachi Digital is a wholly owned subsidiary of Hitachi, Ltd. with approximately 35,000 professionals in 27 countries. Hitachi revenues for FY2025, ended March 31, 2026, totaled 10,586.7 billion yen, with 606 consolidated subsidiaries and approximately 290,000 employees worldwide. The release says HARC Compose capabilities are expected to expand as Hitachi Digital grows its technical talent base and ecosystem alliances. The release does not give pricing, customer names, or a general availability date beyond saying deployments are underway. More to follow.

stories.Headline: AI linked stocks drop as investors worry over Anthropic revenue growth and new chip export rules
stories.Summary:
Several artificial intelligence linked stocks experienced significant price drops during an afternoon trading session on November 20, 2026. DigitalOcean saw the steepest decline of 13.2 percent, while Oracle and C3.ai both fell by approximately 8 percent. Snowflake shares decreased by 5.3 percent, and SentinelOne shares dropped by 4.7 percent. These losses followed a more than 10 percent slide for Anthropic after its initial public offering.

The market reaction followed an 81.3 billion dollar initial public offering for Anthropic and quarterly earnings results from Nvidia under interim CEO Colette Kress. Investors grew concerned that Anthropic would not meet the fast revenue growth required to justify its 83 dollar offer price. Additionally, the Commerce Department Bureau of Industry and Security now requires licenses for advanced chips sent to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. These rules aim to stop Chinese firms from leasing Nvidia compute resources in those foreign countries.

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying interest rate hikes before an expected increase in December. Governor Michael S. Barr stated that on-balance-sheet debt for the seven largest AI firms could exceed 800 billion dollars by the end of the year. He further noted that nominal guarantees and off-balance-sheet leases for these companies might top 3 trillion dollars. President Donald Trump also added to the volatility by threatening penalties on data centers built outside the United States.

The current downturn follows a period of extreme volatility for companies like DigitalOcean, which reached a 52-week high of 181.29 dollars in June 2026. Market analysts suggest that selling pressure on major artificial intelligence leaders often spreads to other software and semiconductor companies. Future capital flows and unit economics for the sector will likely be tested by upcoming financial results. Investors are now monitoring whether these price drops represent buying opportunities for high-quality stocks.

stories.Headline: Google blocks 41 AI crawlers from accessing Google Maps pages
stories.Summary:
Google updated its robots.txt file on google.com to block 41 AI crawlers from accessing Google Maps pages. This change occurred between November 17 and November 22, 2026, according to an analysis of archived files. The company placed these bots under a shared AI training opt-out token. Google's own AI control, Google-Extended, remains in the default group to keep Maps open.

The new rules apply to 41 named crawlers, including OpenAI's GPTBot, Anthropic's ClaudeBot, and ByteDance's Bytespider. These bots are now shut out of every Google Maps page on the domain. The group uses the __usage_ai-training token, which Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic committed to honor on October 30, 2026. The list includes Japanese bots Cotoyogi and SBIntuitionsBot, as well as Applebot-Extended and img2dataset.

Japanese SEO specialist Masahiro Tsuji first flagged the update in a post on X at 14:03 UTC on November 22. He initially claimed Google blocked search results and goto pages, but later revised this claim. Tsuji noted that the update makes the stance of refusing scraping clear in the robots.txt file. He expressed surprise at seeing a crawler from Japanese academic institutions on the list.

Barry Schwartz of Search Engine Roundtable replied that some of these rules were added back in July. The change affects various model builders, including Amazonbot, Meta's FacebookBot, and developers from China like DeepSeekBot and QwenBot. Other affected entities include Mistral, Cohere, the Allen Institute for AI, and the Common Crawl archive. These crawlers now lose access to business listings, directions, and contributor profiles on Maps.

The robots.txt file uses a protocol where crawlers follow the most specific user agent group that matches them. Google rewrote an internal comment to ensure new named groups are paired with either the default or AI training group. This design prevents the default group's longer allow rules from overriding the training group's single disallow for maps. Most other pages, like search results, were already off limits to every crawler.

Microsoft will begin honoring these training preferences on February 1, 2027, based on the shared token. Google plans to support the token in early 2027, though private agreements may override these rules. The draft specification states that the policy token is not a directive for crawling behavior. The articles leave open why Google split its own Gemini control from the other 41 bots.

stories.Headline: US export rules restrict a wider range of chips including those for consumer electronics
stories.Summary:
The United States government introduced tighter export controls on Thursday, November 20, 2026, to restrict the flow of semiconductor technology. Industry insiders report that these new rules are causing a much wider disruption across the global supply chain than was first anticipated. The restrictions are not limited to advanced artificial intelligence chips but also impact system on chips used in common consumer electronics. Consequently, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. has already suspended some of its shipments to various clients.

These updated regulations affect a diverse range of developers, including those who are not based in China and do not create AI hardware. The rules target mobile and everyday consumer applications, which forces companies to change how they source and distribute their semiconductor components. Because the world's largest contract chipmaker is involved, the changes impact major customers like Nvidia who rely on leading-edge processors. Every developer using these specific types of integrated circuits must now navigate these stricter American trade requirements.

Multiple industry executives told Nikkei Asia that the scope of these controls is unexpectedly broad and damaging to the supply chain. They expressed concern that the rules extend far beyond the intended targets of high-end AI technology to hit general electronics. These leaders believe the current environment creates significant uncertainty for developers who were previously unaffected by trade wars. They warned that the sudden suspension of shipments could lead to larger shortages of essential components for mobile devices.

stories.Headline: Yasir Mahmood lists ways to access paid AI models for free through developer tools and student offers
stories.Summary:
Yasir Mahmood, a mechanical engineer and technology writer for MakeUseOf, published a guide on November 22, 2026, regarding free access to paid artificial intelligence models. He noted that free chatbot options became more restrictive throughout 2026, including the October 2026 move by Google to shift free Gemini app accounts to Flash-Lite. Additionally, the free sign-in options for Gemini CLI and Qwen Code were ended entirely during this period.

Users can access Gemini 4 Hydrogen, released on November 12, 2026, for free through Google AI Studio without providing a credit card. GitHub Copilot Free offers 2,000 monthly inline code completions and uses Copilot Fusion to route tasks to models like GPT-6 Luna. OpenRouter provides 11 free models as of November 22, 2026, allowing 50 free requests per day for users who skip the payment method. Eligible United States college students aged 18 or older can claim 12 months of Google AI Pro, worth 19.99 dollars monthly, if they redeem the offer by December 31, 2026.

Yasir explained that while these routes work, they each have specific drawbacks that users should consider before relying on them. He warned that Google AI Studio may use prompts for training purposes, and OpenRouter models can disappear without notice as promotions end. For the student offer, he advised setting a reminder because Google will charge the monthly fee after the free year expires. He suggested that AI Studio is best for general prompts, while Copilot Free is the strongest choice for coding tasks.

The author noted that free access is now primarily found through developer tools and student promotions rather than standard chatbot applications. He mentioned that GitHub Education provides free Copilot access for verified students, though sign-ups were paused from April until June 2026. He also clarified that a previous offer for four months of free ChatGPT Plus for students ended on October 31. stories.Headline: Governor Kathy Hochul pauses a proposed AI data center project in Niagara Falls
stories.Summary:
Governor Kathy Hochul paused a proposed artificial intelligence data center project in Niagara Falls. She signed an executive order on July 14, 2026, to freeze certain permits. This action affects the Niagara Digital Campus proposed by Niagara Falls Redevelopment. The developer first proposed this specific data center project back in 2021. The freeze on state environmental permits can last for up to one year.

The project requires a state air permit for backup diesel generators and costs 1.5 billion dollars. It involves nine buildings using 140 megawatts near the Robert Moses plant. The Milstein family owns Niagara Falls Redevelopment, which wants to build on vacant South End land. National Grid confirmed in 2023 that transmission lines could accommodate the 140 megawatts. The developer requested an interconnection from the New York Independent System Operator in April 2024.

Governor Hochul said the pause allows the state to study effects on water and electric bills. She stated that developers should pay for the infrastructure they require rather than households. Niagara Falls Redevelopment says it will pay for its own grid upgrades and substation. The state council of building trades urged the governor not to adopt the freeze. A consultant projects 675 annual construction jobs and 550 permanent positions for the campus.

Opponents of the project expressed worries about noise, water use, and higher electric bills. Residents across the country have fought data centers over water and power bills. A noise study by the developer concluded sound levels at nearby residences would not increase. The builder, Urbacon, designs cooling systems that use little or no water for the facility. The project would use city sewers and water, which the sewer district can accommodate.

China added 543 gigawatts of generating capacity in 2025, mostly through wind and solar power. The U.S. faces a projected 44 gigawatt power shortfall for data centers by 2028. In early 2026, local opposition delayed 75 American data center projects worth 130 billion dollars. China's data centers pay about 3 cents per kilowatt hour, which is one third of American prices. Stanford University found American and Chinese chatbots were nearly equal by March 2026.

The State Legislature passed the Responsible Data Center Development Act to pause permits for 20 megawatts. Governor Hochul has until December 31 to act on this broader legislative restriction. The project's target date for interconnection was June 2027, but the current freeze creates delays. The articles leave open whether the project will move to Virginia, Texas, or Ohio. It remains undecided if the state will impose conditions or reject the project entirely.

stories.Headline: Senators question whether Meta's AI data centers qualify for $6.6 billion in research tax credits
stories.Summary:
A New York Times article has renewed attention on the tax credits that Meta claimed for its artificial intelligence data centers, according to a report published by Accounting Today on November 20, 2026. In a letter dated October 14, 2026, Senate Finance Committee ranking member Ron Wyden of Oregon and six other senators said Meta claimed about $6.6 billion in federal research and development tax credits between 2023 and 2025. The senators questioned whether Meta described its AI data centers as experimental pilot models in those claims and asked the company for a breakdown of the credits tied to the data centers. The inquiry highlights two separate questions, which are whether the development activities count as qualified research and whether the claimed expenditures count as qualified research expenditures for the credit. Treasury Regulation 1.174-2(a)(4) defines a pilot model as any representation or model of a product that is produced to evaluate and resolve uncertainty about the product during its development or improvement.

The rules say production costs paid or incurred after the uncertainty is eliminated are not eligible, and a pilot model must involve genuine uncertainty in the design that the model is needed to resolve. Meeting that definition does not by itself satisfy Section 41 of the tax code, which sets additional requirements for the credit and for eligible expenses. Only wages, supplies, computer leasing and contractor costs tied to qualifying research activities can be claimed as qualified research expenses. Section 41(b)(2)(C) excludes land, improvements to land and property subject to depreciation from the definition of qualified supplies, so a taxpayer cannot turn depreciable equipment into qualified supplies by calling it experimental or by not claiming depreciation on it.

For Meta's data centers, the treatment of purchased servers, chips and other equipment is a central issue, because using equipment for qualified research does not by itself make its purchase price a qualified supply expense. Meta asserts that uncertainty existed in the data centers and that it could only be resolved by building a physical data center and testing it. To support that claim, Meta would need to show the technical uncertainty that existed before the data center was built and how building it resolved that uncertainty. The article says taxpayers claiming pilot model costs should build a record that connects the technical work to the claimed expenditures, including initial design questions, alternative designs, simulation results, test plans, test findings and engineering designs.

Cost records for employee activities, materials and contractor charges should be traceable to the relevant development work and should complement the technical evidence. The article, written by David Seibel, a senior manager in the research and development tax credit practice at Indianapolis-based McGuire Sponsel, says the credit is one of the most fact-intensive and subjective areas of tax law. It says the questions raised by the Meta claim extend well beyond AI infrastructure, because manufacturers, equipment developers and other businesses face similar challenges in showing why a model was built, how its development involved experimentation and which costs the credit permits. The articles do not say what happens next in the Senate inquiry or whether Meta has responded to the senators' request.

stories.Headline: Council of Europe trains 20 local authority teams to govern AI responsibly
stories.Summary:
The Congress of Local and Regional Authorities of the Council of Europe organised the first-ever Academy on responsible AI governance at local level, held in Paris from 17 to 19 November 2026. Twenty teams from local and regional authorities, selected in an open call, took part in the academy. The teams came from 18 municipalities and two counties, spanning the continent from Diyarbakır in Türkiye to Fingal in Ireland. The academy was organised by the Centre of expertise for multilevel governance (CEMG) at the Congress, in partnership with the Council of Europe's Steering Committee for new and emerging digital technologies (CDNET). It put into practice the Congress's call to strengthen local and regional authorities' capacity to use and manage AI.

Participants were provided with practical tools for responsible AI governance, based on the Council of Europe's HUDERIA methodology for assessing the impact of AI systems. Over three days, participants applied the methodology to a fictional AI-supported public consultation, identifying and analysing risks, mapping stakeholders and developing mitigation measures. The programme was designed to strengthen authorities' capacity to assess the impact of AI in public services on everyone they serve, from a human-rights, democracy and rule-of-law perspective. The participating authorities were Amaroussion (Greece), Bălți (Republic of Moldova), Bergen (Norway), Bitola (North Macedonia), City of Arezzo (Italy), City of Vigo (Spain), Diyarbakır (Türkiye), Fingal County (Ireland), Harghita County (Romania), Kutaisi (Georgia), London Borough of Camden (United Kingdom), Lviv (Ukraine), Nõo (Estonia), Resen (North Macedonia), Rivne (Ukraine), Shkodër (Albania), Szentendre (Hungary), Turnišče (Slovenia), Valongo (Portugal), and Ventspils Education Board (Latvia). The academy was also an official part of the "Road to Geneva" programme, leading up to the 2027 Geneva AI summit.

Opening the discussions, Congress co-rapporteur on AI Annika Vaikla (Estonia, ILDG), Deputy Mayor of Viimsi, urged authorities to use AI to give public servants more time for people, while keeping people in control. She called for AI literacy among political leaders, staff and citizens. She also called for smaller municipalities to have access to shared expertise. Deputy Mayor Vaikla is co-rapporteur for the 2026 Congress report on strengthening the capacities of local and regional authorities in the use of artificial intelligence. The articles give no further remarks from her.

The articles state that local and regional authorities are on the frontline of the AI revolution in Europe's town halls. Faced with shrinking budgets, they see real potential in efficiency gains promised by AI. They also face hard questions such as planning applications for data centres and democratic accountability for decisions informed by AI. The articles say they lack capacity in understanding and governing AI technologies, particularly smaller municipalities.

The academy served as a Congress contribution to the Council of Europe's New Democratic Pact for Europe and was held in support of the implementation of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence. The articles give no further background beyond the academy's organisation and aims. They state that artificial intelligence is already in Europe's town halls. They describe the academy as the first-ever of its kind at local level.

They state that the twenty teams were selected in an open call. They state that the programme was designed to strengthen authorities' capacity to assess the impact of AI in public services. They give no further details on the Congress report or the Framework Convention. The articles state that the academy was an official part of the "Road to Geneva" programme, leading up to the 2027 Geneva AI summit.

They state that it was held in support of the implementation of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence. They state that it served as a Congress contribution to the Council of Europe's New Democratic Pact for Europe. They give no further details on what follows the academy. They leave open what the participating authorities will do next and what the 2026 Congress report will contain.

stories.Headline: NSPCC campaign addresses how under-16s are protected from and prepared for AI
stories.Summary:
The Times published a report on 22 November 2026 asking what school children hope and fear about artificial intelligence, framed around questions of cheating and deepfakes. The article describes how the question of protecting under-16s from new technology while also helping them to use it is being addressed through an NSPCC campaign. Alice Thomson, writing for the paper, saw how students reacted to that campaign. The piece sets out the tension between guarding young people against harm and equipping them to work with the tools.

The report presents the issue as a choice between protection and preparation, asking how under-16s should be shielded from new technology and helped to use it at the same time. It names cheating and deepfakes as among the concerns the discussion covers. The NSPCC campaign is described as the vehicle for addressing the issue, and the article follows Thomson as she observes students responding to it. No further figures, dates or names appear in the available text.

Responsibility for the issue is placed with the NSPCC, whose campaign the article says hopes to address it, and with the wider question of how under-16s should be protected and helped. The article does not record what the students themselves said, so their views are not set out in the text available. Thomson's role is limited to seeing how the students reacted to the campaign. The paper frames the matter as one of balancing protection against preparation.

The context given is the arrival of new technology, with cheating and deepfakes cited as the specific worries in view. The article does not say what happens next, beyond the campaign's stated hope of addressing the issue. It offers no timetable, no figures and no further named individuals. More to follow.

stories.Headline: IT leaders prioritize data streaming over AI to feed real-time systems, Confluent survey finds
stories.Summary:
IT leaders are now prioritizing the infrastructure that feeds artificial intelligence over the technology itself, according to a report released on November 22, 2026. This shift indicates that enterprises are focusing on data streaming platforms to ensure information moves continuously rather than remaining locked in disconnected systems. The trend suggests that organizations are becoming more realistic about the foundational work required to make advanced technology successful.

The 2026 Data Streaming Report from Confluent surveyed 4,625 IT leaders across 14 countries to identify these changing strategic priorities. In Singapore, 51 percent of respondents ranked data streaming as a top priority for 2026, while only 31 percent chose AI and machine learning solutions. Security remains the highest overall category at 96 percent, and combined data management, protection, and governance priorities reached 90 percent. Furthermore, 78 percent of leaders reported that insufficient infrastructure for real-time processing is a major challenge, an increase from 62 percent in 2025.

Greg Taylor, the senior vice president and general manager for Asia Pacific at Confluent, stated that investing in data infrastructure is essentially investing in AI outcomes. He noted that 81 percent of respondents struggle with data silos and 76 percent face inconsistent data sources. Taylor suggested that framing infrastructure as a prerequisite for performance is more persuasive than treating it as a separate expense. He emphasized that the real value of data is realized when it is used as and when it is needed.

The report highlights that 97 percent of leaders believe data streaming increases the impact of AI investments. Many organizations are seeing significant returns, with 47 percent of Singaporean firms anticipating at least five times return on investment. Beyond AI, 96 percent of respondents expect benefits in customer experience and 95 percent see a reduced time to market for new services. These findings suggest that real-time data infrastructure supports broader business goals while improving the reliability of live operational decisions.

stories.Headline: Travis Tritt warns fans that AI videos of him commenting on the CMA Awards are fake
stories.Summary:
Travis Tritt posted a warning on social media on the morning of November 22, 2026, after a video that claimed to show his thoughts on that week's CMA Awards went viral and drew hundreds of thousands of views. The video was made with artificial intelligence and carried a watermark disclosing that fact, though the mark was partly cut off in some of the versions that circulated online. In the fake clip, an AI-generated Tritt called the people running the CMA "idiots" for sidelining Ella Langley while celebrating Taylor Swift, who he said did not win a damn thing. The video also claimed that Ella Langley got almost no camera time, which the article calls a dead giveaway that the clip was fake, because she spent much of the show on stage accepting awards for "Choosin' Texas."

Tritt told fans that any recent videos of him supposedly commenting on the latest CMA Awards show are obviously fake and were created using AI, and he asked people to disregard them completely. The article says the fake Tritt video is not even good AI and is clearly fake, yet plenty of people in the replies still fell for it, some supporting the supposed comments and others disagreeing with them. A second AI video is also going around that claims to feature Jason Aldean sharing much the same opinion, bashing the CMA Awards and Taylor Swift, and it has been shared dozens of times and drawn nearly 100 replies from people on both sides of the debate. The article notes that the AI in both the Tritt and Aldean videos is not very good, but that as the technology advances it is getting harder to spot fake content, and people are falling for it regardless.

Tennessee is one of the few states so far that have tried to protect artists from AI-generated uses of their likeness and voice, through a law called the ELVIS Act, which stands for Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security. That law prohibits AI creators from using a person's name, image, likeness, photograph, or voice without consent, and it allows artists and others to sue creators who use their likeness or voice without permission. The article says lawmakers have been slow to respond to the rise in AI, and it calls the problem one that will no doubt get worse before it gets better. Until there are laws not only on the books but actually enforced against the people who make this fake content claiming to be from others, the article says, it is a reminder to verify anything you see online these days.

stories.Headline: Amazon puts an AI agent ahead of manual Brand Store page building
stories.Summary:
Amazon placed an AI agent in front of the manual page builder for its Brand Stores, according to an Amazon Ads Support Center page updated on November 11, 2026. Clicking Add page in the Store builder opens a new window with the Brand Store Builder Agent, a tool that drafts Store pages from typed instructions or from one of six prewritten prompts. A companion page on page templates, updated on November 21, 2026, describes the manual route as the exit from that window. The two pages belong to a set of ten Amazon Ads help articles on Stores, plus Amazon's Brand Registry sales page. Their update dates run from May 1, 2024 to November 21, 2026.

The agent generates content and layouts based on prompts, and brands can choose from six prewritten prompts or write their own custom prompts. Chat can happen in any language, but Brand Store content generates in the marketplace's primary language. A note gives two exits: click Add page without AI Assistance in the upper-right corner or click X in the left-side corner. A separate All Deals tab, updated on November 21, is built and filled by Amazon inside eligible Stores unless a brand switches it off. It uses three named themes with up to 30 discounted products by default, and brands can switch it off or replace it with their own deals page.

Amazon states that the Brand Store Builder Agent is an AI tool that helps create and manage Brand Store pages. Amazon lists three benefits: adding new pages and editing existing pages while following brand store design guidelines, editing any generated content or layout elements to match specific needs, and chatting with the AI agent in any language while content generates in the marketplace's primary language. The page uses three names for one tool: Brand Store Builder Agent in the title, the AI agent in the steps, and the AI Assistant in the single worked example. The Support Center header above all of it now reads Amazon Ads Agent.

The page sets one prerequisite: review if Amazon Brand Registry status is Approved in the Store builder. It describes five steps: click Add page, choose one of six prewritten prompts or write your own instructions in the text bar, review the AI-generated page and request adjustments, click Save and Continue to edit in Store builder, and customize design elements and click Publish. The prompt guide, updated on October 13, 2025, sets out four best practices, each with an example. The Stores moderation guide, last updated on October 9, 2025, states that all assets in a Store go through moderation and must be in the primary language of the locale in which they are delivered.

A separate page, Supported primary language per country, updated on September 2, 2025, lists one language for each of 23 countries. By PPC Land's count, English is the primary language in nine of the 23 countries, Arabic, French and Spanish in two each, and eight other languages in one each. The table names no second language anywhere, so a Belgian Store is assessed in French, not Dutch, and a Canadian Store in English, not French. The table omits Colombia, Chile and Nigeria, which Amazon's own Product Selector guide lists among the 25 marketplaces where that Store module runs. The template page documents three ways to reach the manual templates, and it does not explain why accounts see different controls.

The September 29, 2026 renaming of Amazon's advertising platform around Ads Agent was examined by PPC Land in October. The companion prompt guide carries an update date of October 13, 2025, four weeks before Amazon's unBoxed conference on November 11, 2025, where it announced Ads Agent for campaign building and extended Creative Agent to Streaming TV and Sponsored TV formats. Neither Store page gives a launch date, a list of marketplaces where the agent is available, or a record of what changed in the November 11 update. The Create your Store guide, last updated on July 22, 2026, mentions the agent only as a tip after its template step. The agent page lists editing existing pages as a benefit but gives no steps for it, and step 5 ends at Publish while other guides end at Submit for publishing followed by a moderation review the agent page does not mention.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Google launches AI Max to expand Search ads beyond keywords
stories.Summary:
Google announced AI Max, an enhancement setting for existing Search campaigns rather than a new campaign type, in a post dated 22 November 2026 aimed at advertisers in the UK and wider EMEA region. The feature combines three tools: keywordless Search Term Matching, which uses AI to expand reach beyond manual keyword lists, Text Customization, which uses Gemini models to rewrite headlines and descriptions in real time to match a user's query, and Final URL Expansion, which crawls a site and routes users to the landing page that best answers the query. Google said the setup can capture 15% more conversions by unlocking net-new Search queries and deliver up to 27% more conversions at a similar CPA or ROAS. The post cited over 5 trillion Google searches a year and said habits are shifting through AI Overviews, Lens and AI Mode, with users asking longer and more complex questions.

Advertisers enable AI Max by toggling on "Optimize your campaign with AI Max" in campaign settings or by setting up an AI Max A/B experiment, and Google recommended picking an always-on Search campaign using Smart Bidding with enough budget headroom. Google advised implementing enhanced conversions for leads or Google Tag Gateway in Data Manager, locking in bidding goals such as target CPA or target ROAS, and turning on all three settings together for what it described as a compound effect. It also recommended keeping budgets uncapped or leaving sufficient headroom so campaigns can scale into newly discovered demand. Controls include brand inclusions and exclusions at ad group level, negative keyword lists, and URL inclusions and exclusions to protect sensitive pages, with transparency through search terms and landing page reports.

The announcement was presented by Pauline and Zeina of Google, who said manual keyword lists leave high-intent demand on the table as consumer search behaviour evolves. They described endless manual restructures, duplicating match groups, building dozens of ad variants and mapping landing pages by hand, as hours of weekly work that should go to strategy, and warned that rigid keywords hand valuable customers to competitors. They stressed that advertisers keep total control through the brand and URL settings, and that AI Max is not a campaign type to build from scratch. Google directed advertisers to input brand and URL exclusions and negative keywords before going live and to follow a testing timeline over the following couple of weeks, and pointed readers to Accelerate with Google for announcements, reports, recommendations and training.
